# Loner-Strike: Human-like bots, map & mode tools, and servers for CS 1.6 + CZ (full details)

Loner-Strike is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) desktop app for Counter-Strike 1.6 and Counter-Strike: Condition Zero on Steam. Tagline: "Play Counter-Strike like it's 2004, alone or with the friends you don't have."

Website: https://lonerstrike.com/
Download: https://github.com/jamesontucker/Loner-Strike/releases/latest
Source: https://github.com/jamesontucker/Loner-Strike
Made by: nanoshrine (https://nanoshrine.com)

## Who it's for

People who still play CS 1.6 or Condition Zero, mostly against bots, and want the old community-server experience: classic mods, bots that feel like real players, and a friend joining now and then. Also people who want to run their own CS 1.6 or CZ server without editing config files.

## Requirements

- Counter-Strike 1.6 and/or Condition Zero, the Steam versions. Non-Steam copies are not supported.
- Windows: download and open Loner-Strike; setup finds the game.
- Mac: the Mac version of Counter-Strike can't run mods. Install Windows Steam and the game in CrossOver (paid, free trial), and Loner-Strike finds it there. With Parallels, run the Windows version of Loner-Strike inside the Windows virtual machine.
- Everything it changes is backed up and can be removed from the app.

## Bots

- Bot styles give bots human reaction times, flicks that overshoot, aim that wobbles and sprays that drift, from a newbie lobby to bunnyhopping pros. A mixed lobby gives each bot its own level.
- Each bot has a personality and plays and types to match: it chats, replies to other bots and to people, rages after a run of deaths, and cheers up a teammate.
- A cast of regular bot names with clan tags, and believable pings on the scoreboard instead of "BOT".
- Bots get tilted, panic, make radio calls, spray their logo, and learn new maps by themselves; the included maps and almost every stock map come with ready-made navigation and map knowledge.
- Bot styles: Newbie lobby, Pub server (the default), Mixed lobby, LAN party, Matchmaking, Old-timers, Veterans, Locked In, Hackers and Gods. Or Original, the game's stock bots, unchanged (robotic and predictable).
- Bot settings: difficulty, style, personality strength, lobby mood, how much they chat (Normal to start with), whether they answer people, and players coming and going. Reset bot and fun settings puts them back to the defaults.
- Talk to them in team chat, or by voice on a dedicated server: "rush b", "flash for me", "money?". The Bots page lists what they understand under What you can tell the bots.

## Modes and content

- 22 game modes: Classic, Match (5v5), Deathmatch, Free for all, Gun Game (solo and teams), Zombie Plague (two versions), Warcraft 3, SuperHero, Hide and Seek, Paintball, Deathrun, Base Builder, SoccerJam, Surf, Kreedz, plus knife, pistol, deagle, AWP and scout modes.
- The mods are community classics, patched so they notice CZ bots. Some got bot logic they never had: SuperHero bots pick heroes, SoccerJam bots chase the ball, Roll the Dice bots roll.
- Thousands of maps from GameBanana with screenshots, favorites and search; weapon skins, player models, sprays, effects and HUD; round-end music, Quake sounds (off on a new setup) and classic sound packs. Every Get button opens the GameBanana browser (Get more) on that kind.
- Maps for the game you play: Counter-Strike 1.6 leaves Condition Zero only maps out of its lists, rotations and votes; Condition Zero shows everything.
- Mode voting: players type rtv, vote for the next mode, then for a map that suits it. The host picks which modes are in the vote.
- Add your own maps, sounds and AMX Mod X plugins from a file.
- Mods are downloaded from their original sources and checked against pinned checksums.

## New in 1.0: game modes

- Last Stand (map ls_outpost, best for 4 to 16 players, playable up to 32): co-op; everyone plays Counter-Terrorist and holds a walled desert outpost against waves of creatures (zombies, runners, brutes, spitters, a boss every few waves). Barricades to repair, revives, an armory shop and supply drops. Endless by default, or 5, 10 or 15 waves. Bots defend alongside you. Also set up on de_dust2, de_inferno, de_nuke, de_aztec and cs_office.
- Battle Royale (map br_valley): drop in from high over a river valley with only a knife, loot crates and floor weapons, and be the last one or last squad standing while a six-stage zone closes. Solo, duos or squads of 4. Bots land, loot, hunt or camp by playstyle. Also set up on de_aztec, cs_italy, de_dust2, de_inferno and de_train.
- Bots run deathrun courses (and a bot activator springs the traps) and surf.

## New in 1.0: Tools (Beta)

A Tools section in the app for making things:
- Map editor: brushes, entities and textures in one 3D view (or four, like Hammer), with Unreal, Blender or Hammer camera controls, live checks, prefabs, Hammer .rmf / J.A.C.K. .jmf / .map import (TrenchBroom's too, with its groups and layers) and .map export. Compiles with SDHLT (downloaded on first use; through CrossOver on a Mac) and playtests with bots in one click.
- Game Mode Studio: game modes from Blueprint-style node graphs (over 450 nodes, functions, macros, variables, structs, enums, snippets), compiled to an AMX Mod X plugin; playtest with bots while nodes light up, with breakpoints and live values. NPCs, dialog (Say, Say and Choose, Run Dialog from a table) and interactables for story and RPG modes; the example The Quest Giver shows how. HUD nodes: Status Icon, Objective Marker, Kill Feed Line.
- Plugin Studio: an AMX Mod X editor with suggestions, docs, plain-language compile errors, "Try it in my game", and Export and Import of plugins; loner.inc gives short natives for modes, HUD, players, timers and bots.
- Creature Studio: creature types (zombies, aliens, animals, turrets, bosses) and the waves they come in. Custom creatures go with the maps, modes and prefabs that use them, and can be shared on their own.
- Map tools: Map doctor, Map simulator (bots play a match on a map and a report says where they fight, fall or get stuck), Nav fixer, Callouts and Radar maker.
- Personalize: Crosshair & config, Bot people, Spray maker.
- Watch & inspect: Map viewer (with the bots' nav and what they learned), Replay, Demos, Textures & models.

## New in 1.0: Community and AI agents

- Community browser (Tools, Share): maps, Game Mode Studio modes, prefabs, sprays and textures made with Loner-Strike, hosted on GameBanana (on GameBanana's Technical tab, under Tags, a Custom Tag with the value "LonerStrike"; the title can stay empty; press + and save) and moderated. Try one in a click. Only content and Studio modes can be shared; nothing that runs code is downloaded. Publishing is done from the app, which checks and packages a map with its nav, knowledge and overview, fills in the GameBanana credits and asks whether AI helped make it. Remix a creation with credit to the original; a shared map can carry its editable source. Docs: https://lonerstrike.com/docs#community
- AI agents (Settings): an MCP connector so coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Desktop and VS Code can use the tools. Off by default, local only, read-only until "Allow changes", and it asks before anything destructive. Setup: https://lonerstrike.com/docs#mcp

## Playing with friends

- Seven ways to connect: LAN, your router (port forwarding), playit.gg, Tailscale, ZeroTier, Radmin VPN and Hamachi.
- Server name (up to 63 characters, any language), join password and a ready-to-send invite. Friends only need Counter-Strike, not Loner-Strike.
- A custom welcome page for people who join, and a notification when someone joins while you're away.

## Running a server

- Admins, moderators and VIPs with abilities per role and end dates.
- Moderation: player reports, the chat log, mutes and the swear filter, bans and player history. Stats: ranks and 5v5 match results. Both work for your own game and for each server.
- Map rotation, timed chat messages, AFK and high-ping kickers, stats and ranks, votekick and voteban, join messages with country.
- Match mode for 5v5s (ready-up, knife round, half-time swap), HLTV for spectators and demos, fast downloads, scheduled restarts.

## Dedicated servers and hosting

- Dedicated servers on your own computer (Valve's free dedicated server, downloaded and set up for you), or bring in one you already run.
- Always-on servers on a rented Linux machine (a VPS: Ubuntu or Debian, x86, public IPv4). The app connects over SSH with your key, confirms the machine's identity, installs Valve's server and the mods, opens the game ports and runs it as a service that keeps going without your computer.
- Each server's page has tabs in four groups: Server (Overview, Who can join, Health, Rotation & extras, Spectators & demos, Website status), Game (Modes, Bots, Rules, Fun, Bot voice commands), People (Players, Moderation, Stats, Admins, Welcome page, Shared control) and Library (Mods, Maps, Skins & models, Sounds).
- Who can join: this network only, anyone with the address, or listed on Steam; a join password, a public address, the Loner-Strike server list and how to connect.
- Health: Loner-Strike and Valve updates, the security check (Linux), backup and restore, a daily restart, and Reinstall, Wipe and rebuild or Delete.
- Shared control: friends help run a server from their own Loner-Strike as an Admin or Moderator, even with the owner's computer off (Linux). Tabs their role can't use show dimmed as Owner only or Admins only. Moderators see the ban list and can ban by SteamID for up to a week.
- After that: changes made in the app (settings, admins, mods, maps, sounds) are uploaded automatically, only the files that changed; Valve's server files update from the app; HLTV runs next to it on UDP 27020 and its demos can be copied to your game; the app says when a server stops answering, and why.
- Admins, bans, the swear filter, the welcome page and chat messages can be shared across servers. Mods and other settings stay per server. One server's mods can be copied to another, and your own maps can be sent to a server with everything they need.
- Website status: a small service on a Linux server that gives your website the live player count and a visitor counter, over its own HTTPS or a Cloudflare Tunnel. It also keeps a Discord status message up to date and serves fast downloads.
- Each server has a join password, a console (RCON) password and extra start options.
- The Loner-Strike server list: hosts can put a server on it, and players find it in the app's Find servers (a server browser after Steam's old one, with games on your own network) or on lonerstrike.com.
- Weapon skins and player models per server, under their own names so every player downloads and sees them; the app shows how close each map gets to the engine's limit of 512 models.
- Ports: servers on your computer start at UDP 27016 (27015 is your own game's); on a VPS, 27015 to 27019 for servers and 27020 for HLTV. Open UDP 27015-27020 in the provider's firewall.
- Cost: free on your own computer. A VPS runs from free (Oracle Cloud's Always Free AMD machines, when available) to a small monthly plan at providers like Hetzner, DigitalOcean or Vultr. ARM machines can't run the game server.
- Guide: https://lonerstrike.com/docs#vps

## The app

- Guided setup that finds your game, on Windows or a Mac with CrossOver.
- The sidebar for your own game is grouped like a server's tabs: Game (Play, Bots, Rules, Fun, Add-ons, Rotation & extras), People (Players, Moderation, Stats, Admins, Welcome page), Online (Play with friends, Find servers), My library (Maps, Mods, Skins & models, Sounds, Get more) and Hosting (Servers), plus Tools (Beta). A bar on every page says whether you're changing your own game or a server, with Back to my game.
- Bots, Rules, Fun and Add-ons can be changed before a game starts; changes apply when you start one.
- An in-game menu on F3, and quick actions in the app while you play: pause, round (including Start a mode vote), map, bot count with difficulty and style, god mode, noclip, announce and more.
- Control it from your phone by scanning a QR code on the same Wi-Fi. Actions that delete or reinstall stay on the computer.
- Backup and restore in Settings: everything to one file, or just your game, and daily backups of Linux servers. Signed automatic updates.
- Settings, Help: the docs, Report a problem, Copy diagnostics, and the usual problems with a button to the page that fixes each.
- A built-in radio with twenty-one stations, from drum and bass, jungle, hardstyle, trance and demoscene music to video game music, 2000s hits and nu metal, plus a group of chill stations tagged Chill (ambient, downtempo, space music, vaporwave, chill synthwave, mellow mixes, game remixes and chiptunes) (Bassdrive, Kniteforce, PsyMusic UK, TechnoBase.FM, HardBase.FM, SomaFM, SceneSat, Rainwave, 0nlineradio, Radio Bob, Nightride FM, Radio Paradise), with shuffle and a station list.
- Built with Rust (Tauri) and React. It talks to the game over RCON on your own computer; nothing goes through a server run by the makers.

## FAQ

Is it free?
Yes. The code is open source (GPL-3.0) and every release is on GitHub. Paying on the website is optional and gets you the same download.

Do I need to own Counter-Strike?
Yes, on Steam: Counter-Strike 1.6, Condition Zero, or both.

Does it work on a Mac?
Through CrossOver (Windows Steam inside it), or with Parallels by running the Windows version in the virtual machine. Not with the Mac version of Counter-Strike.

Windows says it protected my PC.
That's SmartScreen, which warns about apps that aren't widely downloaded yet. Click More info, then Run anyway.

Will it mess up my game?
No. Every file it changes is backed up first, and you can remove any mode or all of it from the app.

Do my friends need it?
No. They only need Counter-Strike; the server sends them the maps and sounds.

Do I need a server to play with friends?
No. Your own game hosts them while you play. A dedicated server is for one that stays up when you're not playing.

Who made the mods?
Their original authors: the AMX Mod X, Metamod and ReGameDLL teams and the community modders behind Zombie Plague, Warcraft 3, SuperHero and the rest. Loner-Strike sets them up and patches them for bots. Everyone is credited in CREDITS.md on GitHub.

Is it affiliated with Valve?
No. Counter-Strike and Condition Zero are Valve's trademarks. No game files are included.

## Game Mode Studio nodes (compact)

One line each: Title (type, category): what it does. In: inputs. Out: outputs.

- Round Started (event.round_started, Events): Runs when a round begins: freeze time is over and everyone can move.
- Round Ended (event.round_ended, Events): Runs when a round ends. Winner is no team for a draw. Out: Winner Team, Round number Number.
- Player Killed (event.player_killed, Events): Runs when a player dies. Attacker is nobody when the world killed them (a fall, the bomb). Out: Victim Player, Attacker Player, Headshot Yes/No, Weapon Text, Distance Number, Team kill Yes/No, Suicide Yes/No, Killed by the world Yes/No, Weapon kind Weapon.
- Player Spawned (event.player_spawned, Events): Runs when a player comes alive (each round, or a respawn). Out: Player Player.
- Player Joined (event.player_joined, Events): Runs when a player (or bot) has joined the server. Out: Player Player.
- Player Left (event.player_left, Events): Runs when a player leaves the server. Out: Player Player.
- Bomb Planted (event.bomb_planted, Events): Runs when the bomb is planted. Out: Planter Player.
- Bomb Defused (event.bomb_defused, Events): Runs when the bomb is defused. Out: Defuser Player.
- Bomb Exploded (event.bomb_exploded, Events): Runs when the bomb goes off.
- Player Used (event.player_used, Events): Runs when a player presses a button (func_button) with this name. Leave the name empty for any button. Out: Player Player, Button Entity.
- Player Touched (event.player_touched, Events): Runs when a player walks into a trigger (trigger_multiple) with this name, at most once a second each. Empty name: any. Out: Player Player, Trigger Entity.
- Point Captured (comp.on_capture, Components): A capture point was taken. Out: Point Entity, Team Team, Capturer Player.
- Point Lost (comp.on_capture_lost, Components): A team lost a capture point. Out: Point Entity, Team Team.
- Zone Stage (comp.on_zone_stage, Components): A shrinking zone started a new stage. Out: Zone Entity, Stage Number.
- Zone Hurt Player (comp.on_zone_tick, Components): A player outside the zone took damage. Out: Zone Entity, Player Player, Damage Number.
- Player Extracted (comp.on_extract, Components): A player got out at an extraction point. Out: Point Entity, Player Player.
- Wave Started (comp.on_wave_start, Components): A wave of enemies started. Out: Wave Number.
- Wave Spawned One (comp.on_wave_spawn, Components): A wave's spawner is about to bring in one enemy. Spawner is the wave spawner, not the enemy (it isn't made yet): to act on its enemies, use For Each Creature (a moment later) or Creature Killed. Out: Spawner Entity, Wave Number.
- Wave Cleared (comp.on_wave_cleared, Components): Every enemy of a wave is dead. Out: Wave Number.
- Crate Opened (comp.on_loot, Components): A player opened a loot container. Out: Container Entity, Player Player.
- Checkpoint Reached (comp.on_checkpoint, Components): A player reached a checkpoint. Out: Checkpoint Entity, Player Player, Order Number.
- Barricade Damaged (comp.on_barricade_damaged, Components): A barricade was hit (Health is what it has left). Out: Barricade Entity, Attacker Entity, Health Number.
- Barricade Repaired (comp.on_barricade_repaired, Components): A barricade was mended a step (by Player; nobody when the mode did it). Out: Barricade Entity, Player Player, Health Number.
- Supply Drop Landed (comp.on_drop_landed, Components): A supply drop came down (it can be opened now). Out: Drop Entity.
- Barricade Broken (comp.on_barricade_broken, Components): A barricade was broken. Out: Barricade Entity, Attacker Player.
- Meeting Ended (comp.on_meeting_end, Components): A meeting ended; Ejected is nobody when no one was voted out. Out: Meeting Entity, Ejected Player.
- Creature Killed (creature.on_killed, Creatures): A creature died. Needs the Loner-Strike bot brain with creatures. Out: Creature Entity, Killer Player, Type Text.
- Is Team (cond.is_team, Conditions): Checks which team a player is on. Nobody (an empty attacker) is on no team, so that goes to False. In: Player Player, Team Team.
- Branch (flow.branch, Conditions): Goes to True or False. In: Condition Yes/No.
- Compare (math.compare, Conditions): Compares two numbers. In: A Number, B Number. Out: Result Yes/No.
- And / Or (logic.and_or, Conditions): Both (And), or either one (Or). In: A Yes/No, B Yes/No. Out: Result Yes/No.
- Not (logic.not, Conditions): True becomes False and False becomes True. In: In Yes/No. Out: Result Yes/No.
- Math (math.op, Numbers): Adds, takes away, multiplies, divides, or picks the smaller or bigger number. In: A Number, B Number. Out: Result Number.
- Random Number (math.random, Numbers): A random number from Min to Max (whole numbers unless Fractions is on). In: Min Number, Max Number. Out: Number Number.
- Health Of (player.get_health, Players): A player's health (0 if dead or nobody). In: Player Player. Out: Health Number.
- Team Of (player.get_team, Players): Which team a player is on. In: Player Player. Out: Team Team.
- Is Alive (player.is_alive, Players): Is the player alive? In: Player Player. Out: Alive Yes/No.
- Is Bot (player.is_bot, Players): Is the player a bot? In: Player Player. Out: Bot Yes/No.
- Name Of (player.get_name, Players): A player's name, as text. In: Player Player. Out: Name Text.
- Count Alive (game.count_alive, Players): How many players of a team are alive (or everyone). In: Team Team. Out: Alive Number.
- Get Variable (var.get, Variables): Reads one of this mode's variables (a per-player one needs a Player, a per-team one a Team). In: Player Player, Team Team. Out: Value Variable.
- Set Variable (var.set, Variables): Sets one of this mode's variables. In: Player Player, Team Team, Value Variable.
- Add To Variable (var.add, Variables): Adds to a number variable (a negative amount takes away). In: Player Player, Team Team, Amount Number.
- Delay (timer.delay, Timers): Waits, then carries on. Paused with the world while debugging. In: Seconds Number. Out: Timer Timer.
- Repeat (timer.repeat, Timers): Runs Each every few seconds, a number of times (0: until the round ends). Then runs at once. In: Every (s) Number. Out: Timer Timer.
- Countdown (timer.countdown, Timers): Counts down on everyone's screen, then runs Done. Out: Timer Timer.
- Stop Timers (timer.stop_all, Timers): Stops every Delay, Repeat and Countdown of this mode.
- Give Weapon (player.give_weapon, Players): Gives a living player a weapon and spare bullets. Does nothing for a dead player, or one who already has that weapon (the debugger marks that). A weapon's name can be wired in (from a data table, say): ak47, deagle, knife... In: Player Player, Weapon Text, Spare bullets Number.
- Strip Weapons (player.strip, Players): Takes a player's weapons away (keeping the knife if you like). In: Player Player.
- Set Health (player.set_health, Players): Sets a living player's health. In: Player Player, Health Number.
- Set Armor (player.set_armor, Players): Sets a living player's armor: kevlar and a helmet, or kevlar only. In: Player Player, Armor Number.
- Set Team (player.set_team, Players): Moves a player to a team (it shows from their next spawn). In: Player Player, Team Team.
- Set Speed (player.set_speed, Players): Sets how fast a player runs (250 is normal) until they switch weapons. In: Player Player, Speed Number.
- Teleport (player.teleport, Players): Moves a living player to an entity: the one wired into To, or the one with this name. In: Player Player, To Entity.
- Show Message (msg.broadcast, Messages): Shows a big message in the middle of the screen, to one player or everyone (no Player). In: Player Player.
- Show HUD Text (msg.hud, Messages): Shows text in a HUD slot, to one player or everyone (no Player). A Value wired in goes after the text. In: Player Player, Value Anything.
- End Round (score.end_round, Scoring): Ends the round now with a winner (no team: a draw). The next round starts after the usual short wait. In: Winner Team.
- Find Component (comp.find, Components): The component (or any entity) with this name. Out: Entity Entity.
- Create Component (comp.create, Components): Makes a component at an entity (wired into At, or the one with this name), with keys like radius=160 capture_secs=8. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright (no Velocity or Scale: a component is a zone). In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector. Out: Entity Component, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Set Zone (comp.zone_set, Components): Sets a safe zone's radius (wire the Safe zone, or the Shrinking zone that drives it), and moves its center to an entity wired into Center or the one with this name (no name: it stays where it is). In: Zone Entity, Center Entity, Radius Number.
- Shrink Zone (comp.zone_shrink, Components): Shrinks a safe zone (or a Shrinking zone's) over some seconds to a new radius, around an entity wired into Center or the one with this name (no name: its center stays). In: Zone Entity, Center Entity, Radius Number.
- Open Crate (comp.crate_open, Components): Opens a loot container for a player. In: Container Entity, Player Player.
- Start Wave (comp.wave_start, Components): Starts a wave (0: the next one). In: Wave Number.
- Stop Waves (comp.wave_stop, Components): Stops the waves.
- Open Extraction (comp.extract_open, Components): Opens or closes an extraction point. In: Point Entity, Open Yes/No.
- Door (comp.door, Components): Opens or closes a timed door. In: Door Entity.
- Set Barricade Health (comp.barricade_set_hp, Components): Sets a barricade's health (0 breaks it; above 0 stands it back up). In: Barricade Entity, Health Number.
- Repair Barricade (comp.barricade_repair, Components): Mends a barricade fully, or one step as if the wired Player held USE on it. In: Barricade Entity, Player Player.
- Roll Loot (comp.loot_roll, Components): Rolls one item from a loot table (configs/gamemodes/loot.ini), only items of this tier or lower (0: any). In: Tier Number. Out: Item Text, Rolled Yes/No.
- Next Zone Stage Now (comp.zone_skip, Components): A Shrinking zone goes to its next stage now. In: Zone Entity.
- Fire Trap (comp.trap_fire, Components): Sets off a trap. In: Trap Entity.
- Lock Point (comp.capture_lock, Components): Locks a capture point for some seconds. In: Point Entity, Seconds Number.
- Reset Components (comp.reset, Components): Puts every component back as it was at the start of the map.
- Creature Health (creature.health, Creatures): A creature's health now (0 when it's gone). In: Creature Entity. Out: Health Number.
- Spawn Creature (creature.spawn, Creatures): Makes a creature of this type at an entity (wired into At, or the one with this name). Needs the Loner-Strike bot brain with creatures (the debugger says so if not). If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. In: At entity Entity, Health Number, Pay Number, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number. Out: Entity Creature, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Player Hurt (event.player_hurt, Events): Runs when a player takes damage, with the health it took (blocked damage doesn't count). Hit Position: where a bullet or the knife struck (else the middle of the victim); Direction: which way the hit was going (from the attacker). Use Get Transform on Victim/Attacker for where they were. Out: Victim Player, Attacker Player, Damage Number, Headshot Yes/No, Health left Number, Hit where Text, Weapon Text, Hit Position Vector, Direction Vector, Hit zone Hit Zone.
- Team Changed (event.team_changed, Events): Runs once when a player joins a team or changes team (Spectator is No team). Out: Player Player, Team Team.
- Map Started (event.map_started, Events): Runs once when the map has loaded (before the first round): load map packs, set things up.
- New Round (event.new_round, Events): Runs when a new round is set up (freeze time starts), before Round Started.
- Chat Command (event.chat_command, Events): Runs when a player says /command or !command in chat (shop for /shop and !shop); Arguments is the rest of the line ("/give 5": 5). Out: Player Player, Arguments Text.
- Function (func.define, Functions): A piece of graph you can run from anywhere with Call Function. It gets a Player and a Number from the call. Out: Player Player, Number Number.
- Call Function (func.call, Functions): Runs a Function, giving it a Player and a Number, then carries on. In: Player Player, Number Number.
- For Each Player (flow.for_each_player, Flow): Runs Each once for every player who fits, then Then. Who and Team can be wired (a variable, a Select); Only these goes through a list of players instead (Players In Radius...). Break stops early. For any list of your own, use Arrays > For Each. In: Who Who, Team (overrides Who) Team, Only these Array of Player. Out: Player Player, Index Number.
- For Each Entity (flow.for_each_entity, Flow): Runs Each once for every entity of a kind or with a name (at most 512), then Then. The kind or name can be wired; Only these goes through a list of entities instead. Break stops early. For any list of your own, use Arrays > For Each. In: Kind or name Text, Only these Array of Entity. Out: Entity Entity, Index Number.
- Pick Random Player (flow.pick_player, Flow): Picks one player who fits at random (Found), or runs None. Who and Team can be wired; Only these picks from a list of players instead. In: Who Who, Team (overrides Who) Team, Only these Array of Player. Out: Player Player.
- Pick Random Entity (flow.pick_entity, Flow): Picks one entity of a kind or with a name at random (Found), or runs None. The kind or name can be wired; Only these picks from a list of entities instead. In: Kind or name Text, Only these Array of Entity. Out: Entity Entity.
- Text Is (text.equals, Conditions): Is the text the same as this (capitals don't matter)? In: Text Text, Same as Text. Out: Same Yes/No.
- Stop Timer (timer.stop, Timers): Stops one Delay, Repeat or Countdown.
- Give Money (player.add_money, Players): Gives (or takes, with a minus) money; it stays between 0 and 16000. In: Player Player, Amount Number.
- Money Of (player.get_money, Players): How much money a player has. In: Player Player. Out: Money Number.
- Add Score (player.add_frags, Players): Adds to a player's score (frags) on the scoreboard (a minus takes away). In: Player Player, Amount Number.
- Score Of (player.get_frags, Players): A player's score (frags). In: Player Player. Out: Score Number.
- Deaths Of (player.get_deaths, Players): How many times a player has died. In: Player Player. Out: Deaths Number.
- Give Item (player.give_item, Players): Gives a living player armor, a defuse kit or night vision. In: Player Player.
- Drop Weapon (player.drop_weapon, Players): Makes a living player drop the weapon in their hands. In: Player Player.
- Set Gravity (player.set_gravity, Players): How strongly a player falls (1 is normal, 0.5 half). In: Player Player, Gravity Number.
- Set Glow (player.set_glow, Players): Makes a player glow in a color (or not). In: Player Player, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Set Model (player.set_model, Players): Dresses a player as one of the game's characters (or back to their own). In: Player Player.
- Respawn (player.respawn, Players): Brings a dead player back at a spawn point. In: Player Player.
- Kill (player.kill, Players): Kills a living player. In: Player Player.
- Freeze (player.freeze, Players): Freezes a player in place (or lets them move again). In: Player Player, Frozen Yes/No.
- Set Role (player.set_role, Players): Gives a player a role in this mode (traitor, medic...). In: Player Player.
- Is Role (player.is_role, Players): Does the player have this role? In: Player Player. Out: Has it Yes/No.
- Count Role (game.count_role, Players): How many living players have this role. Out: Count Number.
- Chat Message (msg.chat, Messages): A chat line, to one player or everyone (no Player). A Value wired in goes after the text. In: Player Player, Value Anything.
- Progress Bar (msg.bar, Messages): Shows the game's progress bar filling up over some seconds. In: Player Player.
- Menu (msg.menu, Messages): Shows a player a menu; the choice they pick runs its output (later, when they pick). In: Player Player.
- Set Setting (game.set_cvar, Game): Changes one of the game's settings now. In: Value Number.
- Use Entity (entity.use, Game): Presses (uses) every entity with this name: a door, a button, a trigger.
- Set Player Modifier (up.mod, Upgrades): Multiplies something about a player until they die: max health, speed, reload or swap time (0.6 = 40 % faster), damage, revive time, fire rate (1.25 = 25 % faster). Perks multiply on top. In: Player Player, Times Number.
- Player Modifier (up.mod_get, Upgrades): What a player's modifier is now (the mode's times the perks'). In: Player Player. Out: Times Number.
- Give Perk (up.perk_give, Upgrades): Gives a player a perk (lost when downed or dead). In: Player Player.
- Buy Perk (up.perk_buy, Upgrades): A player buys a perk for its price (1500 + 1000 per perk they have, 4 at most); Bought says if it worked. In: Player Player. Out: Bought Yes/No.
- Has Perk (up.perk_has, Upgrades): Does the player have this perk? In: Player Player. Out: Has it Yes/No.
- Perk Count (up.perk_count, Upgrades): How many perks a player has. In: Player Player. Out: Perks Number.
- Weapon Level (up.weapon_level, Upgrades): The level of the gun in the player's hand (1, 2 Mk II, 3 Mk III). In: Player Player. Out: Level Number.
- Upgrade Gun (up.bench, Upgrades): Upgrades the gun in the player's hand at the bench's prices (or 5000 / 9000). In: Player Player.
- Roll Mystery Box (up.box, Upgrades): The player rolls the mystery box (the one that's out, or the wired one) for its price. In: Player Player, Box Entity.
- Drop Pickup (up.pickup, Upgrades): Drops a pickup at an entity; whoever walks over it takes it (Pickup Taken says what it was). A kind like resupply, doublepay, onehit, airstrike, or anything you handle yourself. In: At Entity. Out: Pickup Entity.
- Perk Bought (up.on_perk, Upgrades): A player bought a perk (at a machine, a shop or Buy Perk). Out: Player Player, Perk Text, Price Number.
- Gun Upgraded (up.on_upgraded, Upgrades): A player's gun went up a level. Out: Player Player, Level Number, Price Number.
- Mystery Box Gave (up.on_box, Upgrades): The mystery box gave a player a gun. Out: Player Player, Gun Text.
- Pickup Taken (up.on_pickup, Upgrades): A player took a pickup. Out: Pickup Entity, Player Player, Kind Text.
- Creature Hurt (up.on_creature_hurt, Creatures): A creature took damage (Headshot when the hit was a head). Hit Position: where a bullet or the knife struck (else its middle); Direction: which way the hit was going. Use Get Entity Transform on Creature, or Get Transform on Attacker, for where they were. Out: Creature Entity, Attacker Player, Damage Number, Headshot Yes/No, Hit Position Vector, Direction Vector.
- Knocked Down On (kd.enable, Downed): On: a hit that would kill a player (of a team, or anyone) knocks them down instead: they crawl and bleed out over some seconds; a teammate (a squad mate, with squads) holding USE for 4 s gets them up with 50 health. Off: nobody new goes down.
- Is Knocked Down (kd.is, Downed): Is the player knocked down? In: Player Player. Out: Down Yes/No.
- Bleed Out In (kd.left, Downed): Seconds a knocked-down player has left (0 when they're not down). In: Player Player. Out: Seconds Number.
- Knock Down (kd.down, Downed): Knocks a player down now. In: Player Player.
- Get Up (kd.revive, Downed): Gets a knocked-down player up (by the wired player, or nobody). In: Player Player, By Player.
- Knocked Down (kd.on_down, Downed): A player was knocked down. Out: Player Player, By Entity.
- Got Up (kd.on_up, Downed): A knocked-down player is back up (By: who helped; themselves for Quick revive; nobody when the mode did it). Out: Player Player, By Player.
- Bled Out (kd.on_bled_out, Downed): A knocked-down player bled out (they die right after). Out: Player Player.
- Open Shop Menu (shop.menu, Shop): Shows a player the shop's menu. In: Shop Entity, Player Player.
- Open or Close Shop (shop.open, Shop): Opens the shop for business, or closes it. In: Shop Entity, Open Yes/No.
- Shop Price (shop.price, Shop): An item's price now (by its name or what it gives); -1 if the shop doesn't sell it. In: Shop Entity. Out: Price Number.
- Shop Purchase (shop.on_buy, Shop): A player bought something at a shop (an @item is the mode's to give here). Out: Shop Entity, Player Player, Item Text, Price Number.
- Talked To NPC (npc.on_talk, NPCs): Runs when a player presses USE on an NPC (after its greeting). Leave the name empty for any NPC. Out: Player Player, NPC Entity.
- Used Interactable (npc.on_use, NPCs): Runs when a player uses an interactable (a lever, a note, a terminal); its map targets fire too. Leave the name empty for any. Out: Player Player, Interactable Entity.
- Say and Choose (npc.choose, NPCs): The NPC (or a narrator, with none wired) says a line and the player picks a reply; each reply runs its output (later, when they pick), and Picked says which (1-6; 0 for none). Timed out: no pick in time. Walked away: they went off, died, left or closed it. Every text can be wired (a variable, a table cell), so one node can run a whole conversation from a data table; Replies sets how many are offered (empty ones are left out). One conversation per player: a new one ends the old (as Walked away). In: Player Player, NPC Entity, Speaker Text, Line Text, Reply 1 Text, Reply 2 Text, Reply 3 Text, Reply 4 Text, Reply 5 Text, Reply 6 Text, Replies Number, Time to answer Number. Out: Picked Number.
- Say (npc.say, NPCs): The NPC (or a narrator, with none wired) says a line to a player, or to everyone with no Player. In: Player Player, NPC Entity, Speaker Text, Line Text.
- Set NPC Behavior (npc.behave, NPCs): What an NPC does by itself: stands, wanders near its spot, patrols its targets, or follows a player (wired into Follow) for a while. In: NPC Entity, Follow Player.
- NPC Look At (npc.look_at, NPCs): Turns an NPC to face a player or an entity. In: NPC Entity, Target Entity.
- Spawn NPC (npc.spawn, NPCs): Makes an NPC at an entity (wired into At), a point, or the entity with this name. Its model is loaded with the map (models/...mdl). If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number, Model Model. Out: Entity NPC, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Spawn Interactable (npc.spawn_use, NPCs): Makes an interactable at an entity (wired into At), a point, or the entity with this name: a model players use (E), with a prompt when they look at it. Once: usable once a round. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number, Model Model. Out: Entity Component, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Spawn Projectile (proj.spawn, Projectiles): Fires a model or sprite (loaded with the map). Where from: At position, else At entity (a player's eyes) moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up (16 forward when nothing is wired there), else the owner's eyes. Which way: Direction, else Rotation, else the way At entity (or the owner) faces when Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset; Velocity, when wired, sets the motion outright. Gravity 0 flies straight; 1 falls like a grenade. Bounces: off walls before it stops. Damage: to what it hits, or everything within Radius (less further out with Falloff). Kills count for the owner. On Hit runs later for this projectile only, with what it hit (each bounce too); On Expired when its time runs out. 64 fly at most; a new round clears them. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. In: Owner Player, At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Direction Vector, Speed Number, Damage Number, Scale Number, Model or sprite Model or Sprite. Out: Entity Projectile, Hit Position Vector, Hit Normal Vector, Hit Player Player, Hit Entity Entity, Hit World Yes/No, Hit Zone Number, Owner Player, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Projectile Hit (proj.on_hit, Projectiles): Runs when a projectile hits something: where, the surface's normal there, what it hit (World: a wall or the floor), and a player's hitgroup (1 head, 2 chest, 3 stomach, 4-5 arms, 6-7 legs; 0 unknown). Out: Projectile Projectile, Owner Player, Hit position Vector, Normal Vector, Hit Entity, World Yes/No, Hitgroup Number, Hit zone Hit Zone.
- Remove Projectile (proj.remove, Projectiles): Takes a projectile away at once (no hit, no damage). In: Projectile Entity.
- Projectile Velocity (proj.velocity, Projectiles): How fast and which way a projectile flies (units a second). In: Projectile Entity. Out: Velocity Vector.
- Set Projectile Velocity (proj.set_velocity, Projectiles): Sends a projectile off at a new velocity (its facing follows). In: Projectile Entity, Velocity Vector.
- Give Healing Item (br.heal_give, Battle Royale): Gives a player bandages (+15 up to 75), medkits (full health) or drinks (+40 over 10 s), up to the carry limit. In: Player Player, How many Number.
- Healing Items (br.heal_count, Battle Royale): How many healing items a player carries. In: Player Player. Out: How many Number.
- Set Armor Levels (br.armor, Battle Royale): Sets a player's vest and helmet levels (1-3; 0 none; keep: as they are). In: Player Player.
- Make Crate (br.crate, Battle Royale): Makes a crate at an entity with these items (loot items: ak47@30@60 bandage:2 vest2). In: At Entity. Out: Crate Entity.
- Rarity Glow (br.glow, Battle Royale): Makes an entity glow in a rarity's color (0 none, 1 white, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 purple, 5 gold). In: Entity Entity, Rarity Number.
- Match HUD (br.hud, Battle Royale): Turns the match HUD on or off (players left, kills, the zone's timer, armor, healing items, the kill feed and the squad).
- Match HUD Words (br.hud_text, Battle Royale): The mode's words in the match HUD in place of the zone's timer (empty: the zone again). In: Text Text.
- Match Feed Line (br.feed, Battle Royale): Adds a text line to Battle Royale's match HUD feed (eliminations, zone news). Not the top-right kill notice: that's Kill Feed Line (Messages). In: Text Text.
- Match Kills (br.kills, Battle Royale): A player's kills this round (counted while the match HUD is on). In: Player Player. Out: Kills Number.
- Drop In (br.drop_in, Battle Royale): Drops a player in from high over a spot (an entity wired into At, else a spread-out landing spot: the map's br_drop markers); they fall slowly and take no damage until they land. In: Player Player, At Entity.
- Landed (br.on_landed, Battle Royale): A player who dropped in is down on the ground. Out: Player Player.
- Squad Lobby (br.lobby, Battle Royale): A lobby of some seconds where people team up (say /squad); then the squads are filled (Lobby Ended). 0: fill them now. In: Seconds Number.
- Squad Size (br.squad_size, Battle Royale): Sets the squad size: 1 solo, 2 duos, 4 squads... In: Size Number.
- Lobby Ended (br.on_lobby_end, Battle Royale): The squad lobby is over and the squads are filled. Out: Squads Number.
- Sides Alive (br.squads_alive, Battle Royale): How many sides have someone alive (squads, and players in none). Out: Sides Number.
- Round Table On (wave.table, Waves): Each Start Wave from now on plans a zombie-survival round on the map's wave spawners: how many (by round and team size), which creature types (unlocked by round, with stand-ins), their health, bosses, packs, heavies, tiers, how many alive at once. A waves.ini section replaces the built-in mix. Creatures hunt players: on, they go for the defenders from anywhere; off, each type keeps its own aggression (a hound only fights what comes near). Flee when badly hurt: Never, they keep coming; Creature's own, each type runs at its own flee point. A waves.ini section (hunt =, flee =) or one wave's line (hunt=0 flee=own) can still say otherwise for its waves.
- Round Table Off (wave.table_off, Waves): Waves go back to the spawners' own settings.
- Round Difficulty (wave.scale, Waves): Times the round table's counts and health (the mode's difficulty). In: Count times Number, Health times Number.
- Alive Cap (wave.cap, Waves): How many creatures at once (0: 16 + 2 a defender, 20-48; never over the game's own cap). In: At once Number.
- Creature Tiers (wave.tiers, Waves): Tiers on (yellow from round 15, red-orange from 20) or off.
- This Round (wave.info, Waves): This round's plan: how many, how many made so far, the health times, whether it's a boss or a pack round (and the type). Out: Planned Number, Made so far Number, Health times Number, Boss round Yes/No, Pack round Yes/No, Boss or pack type Text.
- Kill Pay (wave.type_pay, Waves): What the round table pays for killing this creature type. In: Type Text. Out: Pay Number.
- Creatures Working (wave.creatures_ok, Waves): False once creatures can't spawn on this server (the table fell back to dead players). Out: Working Yes/No.
- Turrets (turret.setup, Upgrades): Turrets: friendly creatures that shoot the horde. A kit (Give Turret Kit, or a shop line with give=turret) is placed with USE where the player looks; bots are offered turret spots at this price. Price 0: off.
- Give Turret Kit (turret.give, Upgrades): Gives a player turret kits to place. In: Player Player, How many Number.
- Place Turret (turret.place, Upgrades): Places a turret where the player looks: from a kit, or paid at the turrets' price. In: Player Player. Out: Turret Entity.
- Turret Kits (turret.kits, Upgrades): How many turret kits a player has. In: Player Player. Out: Kits Number.
- Turrets Out (turret.count, Upgrades): How many turrets a player has out. In: Player Player. Out: Turrets Number.
- Turret Placed (turret.on_placed, Upgrades): A turret was placed. Out: Turret Entity, Owner Player.
- Current Map Name (game.map_name, Game): The map being played (de_dust2). Out: Map Text.
- Next Map (game.next_map, Game): The map the server goes to next (from the map cycle or vote); empty if it doesn't know. Out: Map Text.
- Server Name (game.server_name, Game): The server's name (hostname). Out: Name Text.
- Max Players (game.max_players, Game): How many players the server takes. Out: Max Number.
- Player Count (game.player_count, Game): How many players there are: everyone, people, bots, a team, or spectators. Out: Players Number.
- Game Time (game.time, Game): Seconds since the map started (for timing things: keep it in a variable, compare later). Out: Seconds Number.
- Real Date and Time (game.clock, Game): The server computer's date and time, as text (2026-11-13, 21:30, Friday) and as seconds since 1970. Out: Text Text, Seconds since 1970 Number.
- Current Mode (game.mode_id, Game): This mode's id (as the Game Mode Menu and modes.ini know it). Out: Mode id Text.
- Round Number (game.round_number, Game): Which round this is on this map (1 for the first). Out: Round Number.
- Team Score (game.team_score, Game): A team's rounds won on this map (as the scoreboard shows). Out: Score Number.
- Is Freeze Time (game.freeze_time, Game): Is it the freeze time at a round's start (nobody can move)? Out: Freeze time Yes/No.
- Get Setting (game.get_setting, Game): Reads a server setting (a cvar), as a number and as text: the counterpart of Set Setting. Passwords and the like can't be read. Out: Number Number, Text Text.
- Change Map (game.change_map, Game): Changes the map (if the server has it). The mode changes too only if the next map's preset says so. Asks first when an agent does it.
- Restart Round (game.restart_round, Game): Restarts the round now (scores stay).
- Run Server Command (game.run_command, Advanced): Runs a server console command, like sv_gravity 400 or mp_restartgame 1. Commands that touch passwords, files, plugins or quit the server are refused, and only one command at a time (no ; ). Community modes that use it show "runs server commands". In: Command Text. Out: Ran Yes/No.
- Run AMX Command (game.amx_command, Advanced): Runs an AMX Mod X admin command (amx_slay, amx_slap...). amx_rcon, amx_cvar on passwords, plugin loading, bans and admin edits are refused. In: Command Text. Out: Ran Yes/No.
- Gravity (world.gravity, World): How strongly everyone falls (800 normal). (sv_gravity) Out: Gravity Number.
- Set Gravity (world.set_gravity, World): How strongly everyone falls (800 normal). (sv_gravity) In: Gravity Number.
- Friction (world.friction, World): How quickly players stop sliding (4 normal). (sv_friction) Out: Friction Number.
- Set Friction (world.set_friction, World): How quickly players stop sliding (4 normal). (sv_friction) In: Friction Number.
- Max Speed (world.max_speed, World): The fastest anyone can run (320 normal). (sv_maxspeed) Out: Max Speed Number.
- Set Max Speed (world.set_max_speed, World): The fastest anyone can run (320 normal). (sv_maxspeed) In: Max Speed Number.
- Round Time (world.round_time, World): Minutes a round lasts. (mp_roundtime) Out: Round Time Number.
- Set Round Time (world.set_round_time, World): Minutes a round lasts. (mp_roundtime) In: Round Time Number.
- Freeze Time (world.freeze_time, World): Seconds frozen at a round's start. (mp_freezetime) Out: Freeze Time Number.
- Set Freeze Time (world.set_freeze_time, World): Seconds frozen at a round's start. (mp_freezetime) In: Freeze Time Number.
- Buy Time (world.buy_time, World): Minutes players can buy after the round starts. (mp_buytime) Out: Buy Time Number.
- Set Buy Time (world.set_buy_time, World): Minutes players can buy after the round starts. (mp_buytime) In: Buy Time Number.
- Friendly Fire (world.friendly_fire, World): Can teammates hurt each other? (mp_friendlyfire) Out: Friendly Fire Yes/No.
- Set Friendly Fire (world.set_friendly_fire, World): Can teammates hurt each other? (mp_friendlyfire) In: Friendly Fire Yes/No.
- Team Balance (world.team_balance, World): Does the game move players to even the teams? (mp_autoteambalance) Out: Team Balance Yes/No.
- Set Team Balance (world.set_team_balance, World): Does the game move players to even the teams? (mp_autoteambalance) In: Team Balance Yes/No.
- Team Limit (world.team_limit, World): How many more players one team may have (0: no limit). (mp_limitteams) Out: Team Limit Number.
- Set Team Limit (world.set_team_limit, World): How many more players one team may have (0: no limit). (mp_limitteams) In: Team Limit Number.
- Start Money (world.start_money, World): Money at the start. (mp_startmoney) Out: Start Money Number.
- Set Start Money (world.set_start_money, World): Money at the start. (mp_startmoney) In: Start Money Number.
- C4 Timer (world.c4_timer, World): Seconds until a planted bomb explodes. (mp_c4timer) Out: C4 Timer Number.

- Fall Damage (world.fall_damage, World): Falls hurt (realistic) or not. (mp_falldamage) Out: Fall Damage Yes/No.
- Set Fall Damage (world.set_fall_damage, World): Falls hurt (realistic) or not. (mp_falldamage) In: Fall Damage Yes/No.
- Footsteps (world.footsteps, World): Can footsteps be heard? (mp_footsteps) Out: Footsteps Yes/No.

- All Talk (world.alltalk, World): Can everyone hear everyone's voice? (sv_alltalk) Out: All Talk Yes/No.
- Set All Talk (world.set_alltalk, World): Can everyone hear everyone's voice? (sv_alltalk) In: All Talk Yes/No.
- Time Limit (world.time_limit, World): Minutes before the map changes (0: none). (mp_timelimit) Out: Time Limit Number.
- Set Time Limit (world.set_time_limit, World): Minutes before the map changes (0: none). (mp_timelimit) In: Time Limit Number.
- Win Limit (world.win_limit, World): Rounds won before the map changes (0: none). (mp_winlimit) Out: Win Limit Number.
- Set Win Limit (world.set_win_limit, World): Rounds won before the map changes (0: none). (mp_winlimit) In: Win Limit Number.
- Frag Limit (world.frag_limit, World): Kills before the map changes (0: none). (mp_fraglimit) Out: Frag Limit Number.
- Set Frag Limit (world.set_frag_limit, World): Kills before the map changes (0: none). (mp_fraglimit) In: Frag Limit Number.
- Armor Of (player.armor, Players): A player's armor points. In: Player Player. Out: Armor Number.
- Has Helmet (player.has_helmet, Players): Does the player have a helmet? In: Player Player. Out: Helmet Yes/No.
- Weapon Held (player.weapon_held, Players): The gun in the player's hands (ak47, knife...). In: Player Player. Out: Weapon Text, Weapon kind Weapon.
- Ammo Of (player.ammo, Players): Bullets in the held gun's magazine, and spare ones. In: Player Player. Out: In the magazine Number, Spare Number.
- Has Weapon (player.has_weapon, Players): Does the player carry this weapon? In: Player Player. Out: Has it Yes/No.
- Is Admin (player.is_admin, Players): Is the player an admin (the app's admins: AMX Mod X kick rights)? In: Player Player. Out: Admin Yes/No.
- Is VIP (player.is_vip, Players): Is the player a VIP (a reserved slot)? In: Player Player. Out: VIP Yes/No.
- Ping (player.ping, Players): The player's ping in milliseconds. In: Player Player. Out: Ping Number.
- Steam ID (player.steam_id, Players): The player's Steam ID (STEAM_0:1:2345): the same each visit, for keeping things per player. Bots and LAN players have none (empty). In: Player Player. Out: Steam ID Text.
- Is Spectator (player.is_spectator, Players): Is the player watching (not on a team)? In: Player Player. Out: Spectator Yes/No.
- Time Connected (player.time_connected, Players): Seconds since the player joined. In: Player Player. Out: Seconds Number.
- Player By Steam ID (player.by_steam, Players): The connected player with this Steam ID (STEAM_0:1:2345, as Steam ID gives it), or none; Found says which. Case and the STEAM_0 / STEAM_1 digit don't matter (the same player either way). Bots and LAN players have no Steam ID. In: Steam ID Text. Out: Player Player, Found Yes/No.
- Is Supporter (player.is_supporter, Players): Has the player the Loner-Strike supporter role (from the Loner-Strike Discord, kept in sync by the app: access flag s)? Not the same as Is VIP (a reserved slot on this server). Bots: no. In: Player Player. Out: Supporter Yes/No.
- Player By Name (player.by_name, Players): The player whose name has this text (none: no player). In: Name Text. Out: Player Player.
- Player By Index (player.by_index, Players): The player in this slot (1 to Max Players; none if empty). In: Slot Number. Out: Player Player.
- Gravity Of (player.gravity, Players): A player's own gravity (1 normal; Set Gravity changes it). In: Player Player. Out: Gravity Number.
- Speed Of (player.speed, Players): A player's top speed now (Set Speed changes it). In: Player Player. Out: Speed Number.
- Model Of (player.model, Players): A player's model (Set Model changes it). In: Player Player. Out: Model Text.
- Get Transform (player.transform, Players): Where a player is, where they look (pitch, yaw), how fast they move, and whether they're on the ground or ducking. In: Player Player. Out: Position Vector, Rotation Vector, Velocity Vector, On ground Yes/No, Ducking Yes/No, Transform Transform.
- Set Transform (player.set_transform, Players): Moves a player, turns their view (pitch, yaw) and sets their velocity at once (unwired parts stay). In: Player Player, Position Vector, Rotation Vector, Velocity Vector, Transform (separate pins win) Transform.
- Set Rotation (player.set_rotation, Players): Turns a player's view (pitch, yaw). In: Player Player, Rotation Vector.
- Look At (player.look_at, Players): Turns a player's view toward an entity or a position. In: Player Player, At Entity, Position Vector.
- Slap (player.slap, Players): Slaps a player: some damage and a push. In: Player Player, Damage Number.
- Screen Fade (player.fade, Players): Fills the player's screen with a color for some seconds (white: blinded). In: Player Player, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Screen Shake (player.shake, Players): Shakes the player's screen. In: Player Player.
- God Mode (player.godmode, Players): Nothing hurts the player (or back to normal). In: Player Player.
- No Clip (player.noclip, Players): The player flies through walls (or back to normal). In: Player Player.
- Set Visibility (player.render, Players): How a player is drawn: normal, see-through (an amount), or invisible. In: Player Player.
- Set Ammo (player.set_ammo, Players): Sets the held gun's magazine and spare bullets. In: Player Player, Magazine Number, Spare Number.
- Give Ammo (player.give_ammo, Players): Adds spare bullets for the held gun (a minus takes them). In: Player Player, Bullets Number.
- Remove Weapon (player.take_weapon, Players): Takes one weapon from a player (the others stay). In: Player Player.
- Switch To Weapon (player.switch_weapon, Players): Makes the player take out this weapon (if they have it). In: Player Player.
- Set Kills (player.set_frags, Players): Sets a player's kills on the scoreboard. In: Player Player, Kills Number.
- Set Deaths (player.set_deaths, Players): Sets a player's deaths on the scoreboard. In: Player Player, Deaths Number.
- Move To Spectators (player.to_spectators, Players): Moves a player out of the game to watch. In: Player Player.
- Kick (player.kick, Players): Kicks a player from the server with a reason. Asks first when an agent does it; community modes that use it show "kicks players". (Bans stay with the app's admins: use Notify Admins.) In: Player Player.
- Mute Voice (player.mute, Players): The player's voice isn't heard for some seconds (0: until the map ends). In: Player Player.
- Gag Chat (player.gag, Players): The player's chat isn't shown for some seconds (0: until the map ends). In: Player Player.
- Chat To Team (msg.team_chat, Messages): A chat line only one team sees. In: Value Anything.
- Notify Admins (msg.notify_admins, Messages): A chat line only admins see (for things a mode can't do itself, like a ban). In: Value Anything.
- Entity Class Of (ent.class, Entities): An entity's class (func_door, ls_creature...). In: Entity Entity. Out: Class Text.
- Entity Name Of (ent.name, Entities): An entity's name (targetname) as the map gives it. In: Entity Entity. Out: Name Text.
- Find Entities (ent.find_all, Entities): Every entity of a class or with a name, as an array (at most 512). Looks through the whole map: keep it in a variable instead of in a loop. Out: Entities Array of Entity.
- Spawn Prop (ent.spawn_prop, Entities): A model (models/...mdl, loaded with the map) at an entity's place; solid or not. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number, Model Model. Out: Entity Entity, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Remove Entity (ent.remove, Entities): Removes an entity (never a player). In: Entity Entity.
- Set Entity Position (ent.set_position, Entities): Moves an entity. In: Entity Entity, Position Vector.
- Set Entity Rotation (ent.set_angles, Entities): Turns an entity (pitch, yaw, roll). In: Entity Entity, Rotation Vector.
- Set Entity Visibility (ent.set_visible, Entities): Shows or hides an entity. In: Entity Entity.
- Explosion (fx.explosion, Effects): An explosion at a position: the look and sound, and damage to players within the radius (0: none). In: Position Vector, Damage Number.
- Beam (fx.beam, Effects): A beam of light from one position to another for some seconds. In: From Vector, To Vector, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Set Light Style (fx.lights, Effects): How bright the whole map is: normal, dark, darkest, bright, or flickering.
- Status Icon (msg.status_icon, Messages): Shows, flashes or hides one of the game's own HUD status icons (the buy zone cart, C4, the defuser, the rescue zone...) for a player or everyone (no Player), in a color. Only the icons every player's game has (its hud.txt): for your own pictures use Objective Marker or Show HUD Text. Until death: it goes when they die or leave. In: Player Player, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Objective Marker (fx.marker, Effects): A sprite that floats over an entity (wired into Follow: a player, an NPC, an interactable, a component; it follows it) or at a position, for everyone, one team or one player. The sprite is one of the game's (sprites/arrow1.spr) or your own (sprites/...spr: it goes with the mode, like its other files). Remove it with Remove Marker; it goes by itself when what it follows is gone. In: Follow Entity, Position Vector, Player (for one player) Player, Color (wins over the setting) Color, Sprite Sprite. Out: Marker Objective Marker.
- Remove Marker (fx.marker_remove, Effects): Takes away an Objective Marker (the one wired in, or all of them with none). In: Marker Entity.
- Kill Feed Line (msg.killfeed, Messages): A line in the top-right kill feed for everyone: Killer (or none: the world), the weapon's icon, Victim, and the headshot mark. Only the feed: nobody dies, nothing is counted (Player Killed doesn't run). In: Killer Player, Victim Player, Headshot Yes/No.
- Set On Fire (fun.burn, Players): Sets a living player on fire for some seconds: damage each second (Lit by gets the kill), flames on them. Water or the time running out puts it out; so does Put Out Fire, death or a new round. In: Player Player, Lit by Player.
- Put Out Fire (fun.extinguish, Players): Puts out a player Set On Fire. In: Player Player.
- Trail (fun.trail, Effects): A colored trail behind a player or an entity as it moves (on), or none (off). It comes back after a respawn and when they start moving again. In: On Entity, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Effect Burst (fun.burst, Effects): A burst at a position or an entity: sparks, smoke, blood, a firework, an implosion, a tar explosion, a teleport flash, a lava splash or a colored flash. Count repeats it (up to 10); Color is for the firework and the flash. In: At Entity, Position Vector, Color (wins over the setting) Color.
- Swap Places (fun.swap, Players): Two living players trade places, the way they face and their speed. Not when either would end up stuck in a wall (Swapped is No then). In: Player A Player, Player B Player. Out: Swapped Yes/No.
- Bury (fun.bury, Players): Sinks a living player into the floor up to the chest; they can't walk, but can look round and shoot. Unbury gets them out (also death and a new round). In: Player Player.
- Unbury (fun.unbury, Players): Gets a buried player out of the floor, onto it (never into a wall). In: Player Player.
- Set Camera (fun.camera, Players): A player's view: third person (from behind), back to first person, or the other of the two. Back to first person on death/respawn: on, death ends it; off, they stay in third person through deaths and respawns. Leaving always ends it. In: Player Player.
- Is Third Person (fun.is_third, Players): Is the player's view third person (Set Camera)? In: Player Player. Out: Third person Yes/No.
- View From (fun.view_from, Players): A cinematic view: the chosen players (the wired one, a team or everyone; each gets a camera of their own) see from a position and angles, or from an entity (following it, Offset above it), for some seconds (0: until Return View). Look at: an entity or position it keeps pointing at (its angles worked out, over Angles). Move to: it glides there over Move time. Frame a conversation: with the wired player and an NPC in Look at, the camera stands to the side of both, looking at the NPC (for Say and Choose); Until the conversation ends gives the view back when it does. Death, leaving and a new round give the view back by themselves. Freeze: they can't move or shoot meanwhile. A map's own trigger_camera still works. In: Player Player, From entity Entity, Position Vector, Angles Vector, Move to Vector, Move to angles Vector, Look at Entity, Look at position Vector.
- Return View (fun.view_return, Players): Gives back the normal view (first or third person, as Set Camera left it) after View From: to the wired player, or everyone viewing. In: Player Player.
- Drunk View (fun.drunk, Players): Wobbles a player's view for some seconds, gently (1) to wildly (10); it stops cleanly (also on death). In: Player Player.
- As Player (cast.player, Players): Casting: is this entity a player (a slot 1-32 that's connected, bots too)? Success with it as a Player, else Failed. Use it where an Entity wire should go into a Player pin. In: Entity Entity. Out: Player Player.
- As Creature (cast.creature, Creatures): Casting: is this entity one of the bot brain's creatures? Success with it as a Creature (and its type), else Failed. In: Entity Entity. Out: Creature Creature, Type Text.
- Is NPC (ent.is_npc, Entities): Casting: is the entity an NPC (ls_npc)? In: Entity Entity. Out: NPC Yes/No.
- Is Interactable (ent.is_interactable, Entities): Casting: is the entity an interactable (ls_interactable, a point or a brush)? In: Entity Entity. Out: Interactable Yes/No.
- Kind Of (ent.kind_of, Entities): Casting: what the entity is, as the built-in Entity Kind enum: Player, Bot, Creature, NPC, Interactable, Component, Prop (Spawn Prop's), Map entity or None. Wire it into Switch on Enum: one output per kind, nothing to type. In: Entity Entity. Out: Kind Entity Kind.
- Component Kind Of (ent.comp_kind, Entities): Casting: which kind of game mode component the entity is, as the built-in Component Kind enum (capture point, shop, barricade, timed door...), or None. Wire it into Switch on Enum for one output per kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: Component kind Component Kind.
- Is Component (ent.is_component, Entities): Casting: is the entity a game mode component (any, or of one kind: a capture point, a shop, a barricade...)? In: Entity Entity. Out: Component Yes/No.
- Call Plugin Function (amx.call, Advanced): Calls a public function in another AMX Mod X plugin (by its file, like gm_components.amxx) with up to two numbers; Result is what it returns. Community modes that use it show "calls other plugins". In: Argument 1 Number, Argument 2 Number. Out: Result Number, Called Yes/No.
- Plugin Is Running (amx.plugin_running, Advanced): Is this AMX Mod X plugin loaded and running? Out: Running Yes/No.
- Fire Custom Event (amx.fire, Advanced): Sends an event with a name and two numbers that other plugins (and other Studio modes, with On Custom Event) can listen to (forward ls_studio_event(name[], a, b)). In: A Number, B Number.
- On Custom Event (amx.on_event, Advanced): Runs when this mode or another plugin fires a custom event with this name. Out: A Number, B Number.
- Player Said (event.player_said, Events): Runs when a player chats (anything; Team Only for team chat). Out: Player Player, Text Text, Team only Yes/No.
- Freeze Time Ended (event.freeze_ended, Events): Runs when the freeze time ends and players can move.
- Map Ending (event.map_ending, Events): Runs when the map ends (the scoreboard shows), just before the next map.
- Weapon Fired (event.weapon_fired, Events): Runs when a player shoots (at most 10 times a second per player). Frequent: keep the flow short. Out: Player Player, Weapon Text.
- Reloaded (event.reloaded, Events): Runs when a player starts reloading. Out: Player Player, Weapon Text.
- Hostage Rescued (event.hostage_rescued, Events): Runs when a player rescues a hostage. Out: Player Player.
- VIP Escaped (event.vip_escaped, Events): Runs when the VIP escapes. Out: Player Player.
- Bots: Phase (bots.phase, Bots): Tells the bots what part of the game it is: Loot (nobody is an enemy: they gear up and keep apart), Fight, or back to normal. Personality influence: 0 they obey exactly; 50 as usual; 100 each bot's personality and skill decide (a careful one may turn a risky job down, a slow one starts later). In: Personality influence Number.
- Bots: Don't Buy (bots.no_buy, Bots): Bots skip buying (they leave the buy time at once and get on with the mode), or buy again. In: Don't buy Yes/No.
- Bots: Friends (bots.friends, Bots): Makes two groups friends for the bots (they won't attack each other and may stick together), or not. A tag is set with Bots: Tag. In: Player A Player, Player B Player, Friends Yes/No.
- Bots: Tag (bots.tag, Bots): Gives a player a tag (a squad, a job) so other Bots nodes can name them all at once. In: Player Player.
- Bots: Prefer Layer (bots.layer, Bots): Bots look for loot and hold on this layer of the map: below (tunnels, basements), the surface, or high (roofs, ridges); or their own choice again. Personality influence: 0 they obey exactly; 50 as usual; 100 each bot's personality and skill decide (a careful one may turn a risky job down, a slow one starts later). In: Bot Player, Personality influence Number.
- Bots: Fight Creatures (bots.creature_enemies, Bots): Bots treat the mode's creatures as enemies (on by default where creatures attack), or not. In: Fight them Yes/No.
- Bots: Goal (bots.goal, Bots): Gives bots something to do at an entity: defend or capture it, use it (hold USE), loot it, or go and hold there, with a priority (0-100), for some seconds, within a radius. Personality influence: 0 they obey exactly; 50 as usual; 100 each bot's personality and skill decide (a careful one may turn a risky job down, a slow one starts later). In: Bot Player, At Entity, Priority Number, For (seconds) Number, Personality influence Number.
- Bots: Clear Goals (bots.goal_clear, Bots): Takes back goals given with Bots: Goal (all of them, or one kind). In: Bot Player.
- Bots: Offer (bots.offer, Bots): Tells bots something here can be bought or used for a price (a perk, an upgrade bench, a mystery box, a trap, a turret spot); they take it like a person would, when they can afford it and it's calm. Personality influence: 0 they obey exactly; 50 as usual; 100 each bot's personality and skill decide (a careful one may turn a risky job down, a slow one starts later). In: Bot Player, At Entity, Price Number, Personality influence Number.
- Bots: Clear Offer (bots.offer_clear, Bots): Takes back an offer (it's bought or used up), or all of them. In: Bot Player, At Entity.
- Bot Go To (bot.goto, Bots): Sends a bot to the entity with this name (it still fights on the way), for some seconds (0: until freed). In: Bot Player.
- Bot Hold (bot.hold, Bots): Makes a bot hold where it is for some seconds. In: Bot Player, Seconds Number.
- Bot Follow (bot.follow, Bots): Makes a bot follow a player for some seconds. Personality influence: 0 they obey exactly; 50 as usual; 100 each bot's personality and skill decide (a careful one may turn a risky job down, a slow one starts later). In: Bot Player, Follow Player, Personality influence Number.
- Bot Nature (bot.skill, Bots): A bot's nature, as the bot brain plays it: Skill, Aggression, Teamwork and Greed (0-100) and its playstyle (rusher, lurker, careful, camper...). People read 0 and empty. In: Bot Player. Out: Skill Number, Aggression Number, Teamwork Number, Greed Number, Playstyle Text.
- Bot Trait (bot.trait, Bots): Is the bot bold, cautious, a team player, a loner, greedy, skilled or a novice (as the bot brain sees it)? False for people. In: Bot Player. Out: Has it Yes/No.
- Bot Free (bot.release, Bots): Lets a bot do as it likes again. In: Bot Player.
- Load Map Pack (comp.load_pack, Components): Loads another mode's map pack for this map (configs/gamemodes/components/<map>.<pack>.ini): br, laststand...
- Start Component (comp.start, Components): Starts a component that waits to be started (a zone shrinker with start_delay -1). In: Component Entity.
- Stop Component (comp.stop, Components): Stops a component. In: Component Entity.
- Barricade Health (comp.barricade_hp, Components): A barricade's health now. In: Barricade Entity. Out: Health Number.
- Zone Stage (comp.zone_stage, Components): The Shrinking zone's stage (the zone or its shrinker); 0 before the first. In: Zone Entity. Out: Stage Number.
- Zone Next (comp.zone_next, Components): When the zone next moves: seconds until it starts (or, while it's closing, until it stops), its next radius, whether it's closing now. Seconds is -1 when nothing is planned. In: Zone Entity. Out: Seconds Number, Next radius Number, Closing Yes/No.
- Is In Zone (comp.in_zone, Components): Is the player inside the zone? In: Zone Entity, Player Player. Out: Inside Yes/No.
- Respawn At Point (comp.respawn_at, Components): Brings a dead player back at a respawn point (ls_respawn_point), or moves a living one there. In: Player Player.
- Call Supply Drop (comp.drop_call, Components): Calls a supply drop onto an entity (wired into At, or the one with this name). In: At Entity.
- Creatures Alive (creature.count, Creatures): How many creatures are alive. Out: Alive Number.
- Player About To Be Hurt (event.player_about_hurt, Events): Runs just before a player takes damage. Block, scale or set the damage here (it happens straight after this flow). Out: Victim Player, Attacker Player, Damage Number, Kind Text, Headshot Yes/No, Hit where Text, Hit zone Hit Zone, Damage kind Damage Kind.
- Block Damage (dmg.block, Damage): The damage doesn't happen. Only in a Player About To Be Hurt flow.
- Scale Damage (dmg.scale, Damage): Multiplies the damage (0.5 halves it). Only in a Player About To Be Hurt flow. In: Times Number.
- Set Damage (dmg.set, Damage): Sets the damage to this. Only in a Player About To Be Hurt flow. In: Damage Number.
- No Fall Damage (player.no_fall, Players): Stops a player taking fall damage: always, or just for their next landing (a drop-in). In: Player Player.
- Make Downed (player.down, Players): A player who just died lies downed where they fell: a teammate (or squad mate) holding USE on them for a few seconds brings them back; if nobody does in time they're out. Bots come to help. In: Player Player.
- Revive Pay (comp.revive_pay, Upgrades): Money for getting a teammate up (the components' downed players: Last Stand, Battle Royale), once a downing, never for getting yourself up; bots get it too. 0: off. In: Amount ($) Number.
- Is Downed (player.is_downed, Players): Is the player downed (waiting for a revive)? In: Player Player. Out: Downed Yes/No.
- Player Revived (event.player_revived, Events): Runs when a downed player is brought back. Out: Player Player, Revived by Player.
- Downed Player Out (event.down_timeout, Events): Runs when nobody revived a downed player in time. Out: Player Player.
- Set Squad (squad.set, Squads): Puts a player in a squad (1 to 32; 0 none). Squad mates are on one side for the bots, and can't hurt each other unless squad friendly fire is on. In: Player Player, Squad Number.
- Squad Of (squad.get, Squads): The squad a player is in (0 none). In: Player Player. Out: Squad Number.
- Squads Left (squad.alive, Squads): How many squads still have someone alive (a living player in no squad counts as one). Out: Squads Number.
