- Squad Friendly Fire (squad.friendly_fire, Squads): Whether squad mates can hurt each other. In: On Yes/No.
- Buying (buy.where, Buying): Where players can buy: anywhere, only in buy zones, or nowhere.
- Allow Buying (buy.allow, Buying): Lets players buy only some things (or everything again).
- Saved Value (save.get, Saved): A number kept for this player across maps, restarts and crashes (0 until set). Each mode has its own file. In: Player Player. Out: Value Number.
- Save Value (save.set, Saved): Keeps a number for this player across maps and restarts. In: Player Player, Value Number.
- Add To Saved (save.add, Saved): Adds to a saved number (a minus takes away). In: Player Player, Amount Number.
- Set Round Clock (clock.set, Round clock): Runs the mode's own round clock: this many seconds, shown on everyone's round timer. When it reaches 0, Round Time Up runs (the game's own time limit is switched off while it runs). In: Seconds Number.
- Add Round Time (clock.add, Round clock): Adds seconds to the mode's round clock (a minus takes away). In: Seconds Number.
- Pause Round Clock (clock.pause, Round clock): Stops or restarts the mode's round clock.
- Round Time Left (clock.left, Round clock): Seconds left on the mode's round clock (0 when it isn't running). Out: Seconds Number.
- Launch Up (player.launch, Players): Throws a living player straight up (with low gravity and No Fall Damage, a drop-in from the sky). In: Player Player, Speed Number.
- Round Time Up (event.time_up, Events): Runs when the mode's round clock reaches 0.
- Function Entry (fn.entry, Functions): Where a Function starts. Its outputs are the Function's inputs (add them in Details).
- Return Node (fn.return, Functions): Ends the Function and hands back its outputs (add them in Details).
- Call (fn.call, Functions): Runs a Function (with its own graph), then carries on with its outputs.
- Call Pure (fn.call_pure, Functions): Works out a pure Function's outputs where they're used (no flow pins).
- Macro Entry (macro.entry, Macros): Where a Macro starts: its inputs (flow and values).
- Macro Exit (macro.exit, Macros): Where a Macro ends: its outputs (flow and values).
- Macro (macro.use, Macros): A Macro's graph, copied in here when the mode is made.
- Sequence (flow.sequence, Flow): Runs each output in turn, top to bottom.
- Do Once (flow.do_once, Flow): Lets the flow through the first time only, until Reset.
- Do N (flow.do_n, Flow): Lets the flow through N times, until Reset. In: N Number. Out: Counter Number.
- Gate (flow.gate, Flow): Flow coming into Enter goes through only while the gate is open.
- Flip Flop (flow.flipflop, Flow): Goes to A, then B, then A again... Is A says which it just did. Out: Is A Yes/No.
- For Loop (flow.for_loop, Flow): Runs Loop Body once for each number from First to Last (at most 10000 times), then Completed. In: First Number, Last Number. Out: Index Number.
- For Loop with Break (flow.for_loop_break, Flow): A For Loop that stops early when flow comes into Break. In: First Number, Last Number. Out: Index Number.
- While Loop (flow.while, Flow): Runs Loop Body while the condition is true (checked each time; at most Limit times), then Completed. In: Condition Yes/No.
- For Each (flow.for_each_array, Arrays): Runs Loop Body once for each item of an array (Break stops early), then Completed. In: Array Array of the node's type. Out: Item The node's type, Index Number.
- Switch on Number (flow.switch_num, Flow): Goes to the output whose case is the number (cases split by commas), or Default. In: Selection Number.
- Switch on Text (flow.switch_text, Flow): Goes to the output whose case is the text (capitals don't matter; cases split by commas), or Default. In: Selection Text.
- Switch on Enum (flow.switch_enum, Enums): Goes to the output for the enum's value. In: Selection The picked enum.
- Is Valid? (flow.if_valid, Conditions): Goes to Is Valid when the entity is there, else Is Not Valid. Any entity handle works: a player or bot, a prop, creature, NPC, interactable, component, spawned entity or weapon (a spawn node's Entity), a map entity. A removed one isn't valid. In: Object Entity.
- Retriggerable Delay (timer.retrigger, Timers): Waits, then carries on; flow coming in again while waiting starts the wait again. In: Seconds Number. Out: Timer Timer.
- Set Timer by Function (timer.by_function, Timers): Runs a Function (with its own graph) after some seconds, again and again if Looping. Its inputs get nothing (0, empty). In: Seconds Number. Out: Timer Timer.
- Set Timer by Event (timer.by_event, Timers): Runs a Custom Event (with no inputs) after some seconds, again and again if Looping. In: Seconds Number. Out: Timer Timer.
- Custom Event (event.custom, Events): Runs when something calls this Custom Event (Call Custom Event, Set Timer by Event, or the map: an ls_event entity, or an info_target named lsev_<its map name>, when triggered). Its inputs are its own (My mode, Custom events).
- Call Custom Event (event.call, Flow): Runs a Custom Event now, with these values (every Custom Event node for it, in the graphs' order).
- For Each Creature (creature.for_each, Creatures): Runs Each once for every creature alive (of a type, or any), then Then. Friendly ones (turrets) are left out. Every creature each time it runs: keep it out of per-frame flows. Out: Creature Entity.
- Creatures of Type (creature.of_type, Creatures): Every creature alive of a type (empty: any), as an array. Looks through them all each time: keep it in a variable instead of in a loop. Out: Creatures Array of Entity.
- Nearest Creature (creature.nearest, Creatures): The creature alive nearest to a point or an entity (a player, a gate), of a type or any; nobody if there are none. In: To point Vector, To entity Entity. Out: Creature Entity.
- Creature Type (creature.type, Creatures): A creature's type (zombie, runner...); empty for anything else. In: Creature Entity. Out: Type Text.
- Idle For (creature.idle_for, Creatures): Seconds a creature has stood still (moved less than 32 units). Counted once a second. In: Creature Entity. Out: Seconds Number.
- Can See (creature.can_see, Creatures): Is there a clear line from the creature's eyes to a player or entity? In: Creature Entity, Player or entity Entity. Out: Sees Yes/No.
- Creature Go To (creature.go_to, Creatures): Sends a creature to a place: an entity wired in (a player, a marker's entity), a point, or the entity with this name. Guard there: it stays and fights there. Then resume: it goes back to hunting once there. In: Creature Entity, To entity Entity, To point Vector.
- Creature Attack (creature.attack, Creatures): Makes a creature go after a player or an entity (a gate, a turret) until it's gone. In: Creature Entity, Target Entity.
- Creature Hold (creature.hold, Creatures): Makes a creature stay where it is (it guards the spot: it still fights what comes close, then comes back) until Resume AI or Go To. In: Creature Entity.
- Creature Resume AI (creature.resume, Creatures): Gives a creature back to its own AI: what its type does by itself (wander, patrol, guard or hunt), its spawn spot as home, no target forced. With an older bot brain it hunts instead. In: Creature Entity.
- Creature State (creature.state, Creatures): What a creature is doing now: 1 idle, 2 wander, 3 patrol, 4 guard, 5 chase, 6 flee, 7 attack, 8 search, 9 dead (0: not a creature). Name gives the word (idle ... dead). Needs a bot brain with creature control 2 (ls_creature_ver 2); the mode says so in the server log when it's older. In: Creature Entity. Out: State Number, Name Text.
- Creature Target (creature.target, Creatures): Who a creature is after now: a player or another creature; nobody when none. Needs a bot brain with creature control 2 (ls_creature_ver 2); the mode says so in the server log when it's older. In: Creature Entity. Out: Target Entity.
- Set Creature Speed (creature.set_speed, Creatures): Times a creature's normal walk and run speed (0.2 to 3; 1 is its own) until it dies. Enraged comes on top. Needs a bot brain with creature control 2 (ls_creature_ver 2); the mode says so in the server log when it's older. In: Creature Entity, Times Number.
- Set Creature Tier (creature.set_tier, Creatures): Makes a creature tier 0 to 3 (2: a yellow shell, 3: red-orange and a bit bigger), as the spawn key tier does; its health keeps its share. Needs a bot brain with creature control 2 (ls_creature_ver 2); the mode says so in the server log when it's older. In: Creature Entity, Tier Number.
- Creature Flee To (creature.flee_to, Creatures): Makes a creature run away to a place (an entity wired in, a point, or the entity with this name). In: Creature Entity, To entity Entity, To point Vector.
- Set Creature Health (creature.set_health, Creatures): Sets a creature's health (and its full health, so it isn't over). In: Creature Entity, Health Number.
- Remove Creature (creature.remove, Creatures): Takes a creature away. Kill: it dies (Creature Killed runs, waves count it; nobody is paid). Remove quietly: it's gone, nothing runs. In: Creature Entity.
- Creature Idle (creature.on_idle, Creatures): Runs when a creature has stood still this many seconds (and, if asked, can't see any player): send it somewhere with Creature Go To. Runs again after as many seconds if it's still stuck. Out: Creature Entity, Idle for Number.
- Get Row (table.get_row, Data tables): Finds the row whose key is this (the table's key column) and gives each of its cells. Found is No when no row has that key (the cells are then 0, No or empty). In: Key Anything. Out: Found Yes/No, Row Number.
- Get Cell (table.get_cell, Data tables): One cell: a column of a row (rows count from 0). Past the end: 0, No or empty. In: Row Number. Out: Value Anything.
- For Each Row (table.for_each, Data tables): Runs Each once for every row of the table, in order, with that row's cells; then Then. Out: Row Number, Key Anything.
- Find Rows (table.find, Data tables): The rows (as row numbers) where a column has this value, in order. Use Get Cell on each. In: Value Anything. Out: Rows Anything.
- Row Count (table.count, Data tables): How many rows the table has. Out: Rows Number.
- Row Keys (table.keys, Data tables): The table's keys (its key column), in row order. Out: Keys Anything.
- Timeline (timeline.play, Timers): Plays a Timeline (My mode, Timelines): values that change over time (a number, a position, a color) and events at set moments. Update runs every tick while it plays; Finished at the end. In a Function with a Player input, each player has their own. Double-click to edit its tracks. In: New Time Number. Out: Forward Yes/No, Time Number.
- Clear Timer (timer.clear, Timers): Stops a timer (a Delay, Repeat, Countdown or Set Timer's handle). In: Timer Timer.
- Is Timer Active (timer.is_active, Timers): Is the timer waiting to run? In: Timer Timer. Out: Active Yes/No.
- Print String (debug.print, Messages): Prints text (and a value wired in) to the server console and the Studio's output, and to chat if you like. In: Value Anything.
- Equal (logic.equal, Conditions): Are the two values the same (or different)? In: A The node's type, B The node's type. Out: Result Yes/No.
- Select (logic.select, Conditions): Picks A when the condition is true, else B. In: Pick A Yes/No, A The node's type, B The node's type. Out: Result The node's type.
- Is Valid (cond.is_valid, Conditions): Is the entity there? Any entity handle works: a player or bot, a prop, creature, NPC, interactable, component, spawned entity or weapon (a spawn node's Entity), a map entity. A removed one isn't valid. In: Object Entity. Out: Valid Yes/No.
- Is Player (player.is_player, Players): Is the entity a player (or bot) in the game? In: Entity Entity. Out: Player Yes/No.
- Is Creature (creature.is, Creatures): Is the entity one of the bot brain's creatures? In: Entity Entity. Out: Creature Yes/No.
- Math Function (math.fn, Numbers): Absolute value, rounding, square root and more; Truncate drops the fraction toward zero (-2.7 becomes -2, where Round down gives -3). In: In Number. Out: Result Number.
- Clamp (math.clamp, Numbers): Keeps a number between Min and Max. In: Value Number, Min Number, Max Number. Out: Result Number.
- Lerp (math.lerp, Numbers): A number between A and B: Alpha 0 is A, 1 is B, 0.5 halfway. In: A Number, B Number, Alpha Number. Out: Result Number.
- In Range (math.in_range, Numbers): Is the number from Min to Max? In: Value Number, Min Number, Max Number. Out: In range Yes/No.
- Number (math.number, Numbers): A number. Out: Number Number.
- Text (text.literal, Text): Some text. Out: Text Text.
- Append (text.append, Text): B straight after A (add a space in B if you want one). In: A Text, B Text. Out: Text Text.
- Format Text (text.format, Text): Text with [0] [1] [2] [3] replaced by the values wired in. In: [0] Anything, [1] Anything, [2] Anything, [3] Anything. Out: Text Text.
- Contains Text (text.contains, Text): Is B somewhere in A (capitals don't matter)? In: Text Text, Find Text. Out: Contains Yes/No.
- Text Length (text.length, Text): How many characters the text has. In: Text Text. Out: Length Number.
- Text To Number (text.to_number, Text): The number written in the text (0 if none). In: Text Text. Out: Number Number.
- To Text (text.from, Text): A value as text: a number, a player's name, a vector, an enum's name... In: Value The node's type. Out: Text Text.
- Find Marker (marker.find, Map markers): The map's marker of this kind (1st, 2nd... in the map's order; a path's spots in their order), where it is, and whether the map has it. In: Which Number. Out: Marker Entity, Position Vector, Found Yes/No.
- Marker Count (marker.count, Map markers): How many markers of this kind the map has. Out: Count Number.
- Marker Key (marker.get, Map markers): A key the map set on a marker (the kit's default when the map left it out), as text and as a number. In: Marker Entity. Out: Text Text, Number Number.
- For Each Marker (marker.for_each, Map markers): Runs Each once for every marker of this kind (a path's spots in order), then Then. Out: Marker Entity, Number (from 1) Number.
- Make Vector (vec.make, Vectors): A position or direction from X, Y and Z. In: X Number, Y Number, Z Number. Out: Vector Vector.
- Break Vector (vec.break, Vectors): A vector's X, Y and Z. In: Vector Vector. Out: X Number, Y Number, Z Number.
- Vector Math (vec.op, Vectors): Adds or takes away two vectors. In: A Vector, B Vector. Out: Result Vector.
- Scale Vector (vec.scale, Vectors): Multiplies a vector by a number (makes it longer or shorter). In: Vector Vector, Times Number. Out: Result Vector.
- Vector Length (vec.length, Vectors): How long a vector is. In: Vector Vector. Out: Length Number.
- Distance (vec.distance, Vectors): How far apart two positions are. In: A Vector, B Vector. Out: Distance Number.
- Direction (vec.direction, Vectors): The direction (length 1) from one position to another. In: From Vector, To Vector. Out: Direction Vector.
- Normalize (vec.normalize, Vectors): The same direction, length 1. In: Vector Vector. Out: Result Vector.
- Position Of Player (vec.player, Vectors): Where a player is: their feet, their eyes, which way they're aiming, what they're aiming at, or how fast they're moving. In: Player Player. Out: Vector Vector.
- Get Entity Transform (ent.transform, Entities): Any entity's place and motion: a player, a creature, a prop, a map entity. Position (a brush entity's middle when it has no origin), Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll; a player's view), Velocity, its box (Mins, Maxs, Center) and whether it stands on the ground. In: Entity Entity. Out: Position Vector, Rotation Vector, Velocity Vector, Mins Vector, Maxs Vector, Center Vector, On Ground Yes/No, Transform Transform.
- Get Entity Position (ent.position, Entities): Where an entity is (a player, a creature, a prop; a brush entity's middle). In: Entity Entity. Out: Position Vector.
- Get Entity Rotation (ent.rotation, Entities): Which way an entity faces: pitch, yaw, roll (a player's view). In: Entity Entity. Out: Rotation Vector.
- Distance Between (ent.distance, Entities): How far apart two things are: each an entity (a player, a creature...) or a point. In: A Entity, Or point A Vector, B Entity, Or point B Vector. Out: Distance Number.
- Direction To (ent.direction, Entities): The direction (length 1) from one thing to another: each an entity or a point. In: From Entity, Or from point Vector, To Entity, Or to point Vector. Out: Direction Vector.
- Position Of Entity (vec.entity, Vectors): Where an entity is (the middle of a brush entity). In: Entity Entity. Out: Position Vector.
- Set Position (player.set_position, Players): Moves a living player to a position (pick one where they fit). In: Player Player, Position Vector.
- Set Velocity (player.set_velocity, Players): Throws a living player: their speed and direction as a vector. In: Player Player, Velocity Vector.
- Make Struct (struct.make, Structs): A struct from its fields. Each field is one value (a number, yes/no, text, a vector, a color, a file (model, sprite, sound or decal), a player, an entity or an entity handle (NPC, creature, projectile...), a team, a timer, a sound loop or an enum); for a list, an Array of the struct. Out: Struct The picked struct.
- Break Struct (struct.break, Structs): A struct's fields, each one value (a number, text, a color, a file, an entity or handle, an enum...). In: Struct The picked struct.
- Set Field (struct.set_field, Structs): Sets one field of a struct variable. In: Value The picked field's type.
- Enum Value (enum.value, Enums): One of an enum's values. Out: Value The picked enum.
- Enum To Number (enum.to_number, Enums): An enum value's number (the first is 0). In: Value The picked enum. Out: Number Number.
- Make Array (array.make, Arrays): An array of the items wired in (a new one each time it's worked out). In: Item The node's type. Out: Array Array of the node's type.
- Players Array (array.players, Arrays): An array of every player who fits. Out: Players Array of Player.
- Add (array.add, Arrays): Adds an item at the end (an array holds at most 10000). In: Array Array of the node's type, Item The node's type. Out: Index Number.
- Insert (array.insert, Arrays): Puts an item in at an index (the rest move up). In: Array Array of the node's type, Item The node's type, Index Number.
- Remove Item (array.remove, Arrays): Takes out every item equal to this one. In: Array Array of the node's type, Item The node's type. Out: Removed Yes/No.
- Remove Index (array.remove_index, Arrays): Takes out the item at an index. In: Array Array of the node's type, Index Number.
- Set Array Item (array.set, Arrays): Changes the item at an index (nothing happens past the end). In: Array Array of the node's type, Index Number, Item The node's type.
- Clear (array.clear, Arrays): Empties an array. In: Array Array of the node's type.
- Shuffle (array.shuffle, Arrays): Puts an array's items in a random order. In: Array Array of the node's type.
- Sort (array.sort, Arrays): Sorts an array (numbers by size, text A to Z, the rest by their number). In: Array Array of the node's type.
- Get (array.get, Arrays): The item at an index (nothing, 0 or empty past the end). In: Array Array of the node's type, Index Number. Out: Item The node's type.
- Length (array.length, Arrays): How many items an array has. In: Array Array of the node's type. Out: Length Number.
- Contains (array.contains, Arrays): Is the item in the array? In: Array Array of the node's type, Item The node's type. Out: Contains Yes/No.
- Find (array.find, Arrays): The index of the first item equal to this one (-1 if none). In: Array Array of the node's type, Item The node's type. Out: Index Number.
- Random Item (array.random, Arrays): An item picked at random (a new pick each time it's worked out). In: Array Array of the node's type. Out: Item The node's type.
- Map Add (map.add, Maps): Puts a value in a map under a key (replacing what was there). In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type, Key The node's key type, Value The node's type.
- Map Remove (map.remove, Maps): Takes a key (and its value) out of a map. In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type, Key The node's key type.
- Map Clear (map.clear, Maps): Empties a map. In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type.
- Map Find (map.find, Maps): The value under a key, and whether it was there. In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type, Key The node's key type. Out: Value The node's type, Found Yes/No.
- Map Contains (map.contains, Maps): Is the key in the map? In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type, Key The node's key type. Out: Contains Yes/No.
- Map Length (map.length, Maps): How many keys a map has. In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type. Out: Length Number.
- Map Keys (map.keys, Maps): An array of a map's keys (a player who left is left out). In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type. Out: Keys Array of the node's key type.
- Map Values (map.values, Maps): An array of a map's values. In: Map Map of the node's key type to the node's type. Out: Values Array of the node's type.
- Reroute (flow.reroute, Flow): A bend in a wire, to keep the graph tidy. Passes on whatever comes in. In: in Anything. Out: out Anything.
- Hide HUD Parts (eng.hide_hud, HUD & View): Hides parts of a player's HUD (or everyone's): the crosshair, money, the round timer, the radar with health and armor (one switch in the game), the weapon and ammo panel, the flashlight icon. Nothing ticked shows it all again. It stays through the game redrawing the HUD; Back to normal on death/respawn ends it there. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Set Field of View (eng.fov, HUD & View): How wide a player sees (or everyone): 90 is normal, less zooms in, more is a fish-eye. A sniper scope still zooms and comes back to this. Back to normal on death/respawn puts 90 back there. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player, Degrees Number.
- Set Weapon View Model (eng.view_model, HUD & View): The model a player sees in their own hands (models/v_...mdl) for the weapon in hand or a chosen weapon, kept whenever they take it out again; also, if set, the model others see them hold (models/p_...mdl). Back to normal model puts the game's own back. Your own models are loaded with the map and go with the mode when you publish it. In: Player Player.
- Flashlight (eng.flashlight, HUD & View): Turns a player's flashlight on or off, lets them use it or not (F), and sets its battery (0 to 100; -1 leaves it). In: Player Player.
- Night Vision (eng.nightvision, HUD & View): Gives a player night vision goggles or takes them, or turns them on or off (giving them first if needed). The same in Counter-Strike and Condition Zero. In: Player Player.
- Silent Footsteps (eng.footsteps, HUD & View): A player's footsteps make no sound (on) or sound again (off). It lasts until turned off or they leave. In: Player Player.
- Scoreboard Tag (eng.score_tag, HUD & View): Shows VIP, Bomb or Dead next to a player's name on everyone's scoreboard (or none: the game's own again). Only the tag: they aren't really the VIP, carrying the bomb or dead. Clear on death/respawn ends it there. In: Player Player.
- Scoreboard Team Color (eng.score_color, HUD & View): Shows a player as a Terrorist, Counter-Terrorist or spectator in everyone's game (name color, scoreboard section) without moving them: their real team, spawns and rules stay. Real team undoes it. Side effects: the radar and name tags follow what's shown, and the player's own buy menu and team HUD do too. In: Player Player.
- Force Spectate (eng.spectate, HUD & View): Makes a dead player or a spectator watch Target through their eyes, and keeps them on Target until Release (or Target leaves). A living player is refused. In: Watcher Player, Target Player.
- Play Soundtrack (eng.soundtrack, HUD & View): Plays a Half-Life soundtrack track for everyone or one player (the game's own music files, as a map's trigger_cdaudio does), looping if asked; or stops it. Players hear it only if their game has the soundtrack (Steam's Half-Life files do). In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Player Pressed Button (in.pressed, Events): Runs when a player presses (or lets go of) a button the game knows: fire, right click, use, jump, duck, reload, walk or a move key. It arrives with the player's ping, like everything they do. Only: wire a player (from a variable) to listen to one player only. Include bots: bots press buttons too. In: Only this player Player. Out: Player Player, Button Text.
- Is Holding Button (in.holding, Input): Is the player holding this button down right now? (What reached the server: it trails their screen by their ping.) In: Player Player. Out: Holding Yes/No.
- Player Command (in.command, Events): Runs when a player uses a console command the mode names (ls_ and letters, like ls_dash): they can bind any key to it (bind f "ls_dash"). Arguments is the rest of the line, as text only: it's never run. Each player can use it at most a few times a second (Player Command uses a second, in the mode's Limits settings). Out: Player Player, Arguments Text.
- Tell Player To Bind (in.tell_bind, Input): Shows how to bind a key to a Player Command: the line to type in the console (bind f "ls_dash"). Nothing is bound for them: the game never lets a server change a player's keys. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Start Cooldown (cd.start, Cooldowns): Starts a cooldown by name (like dash) for Seconds: for each player, each team or everyone. Is Ready says no until it's over. In: Player Player, Team Team, Seconds Number.
- Is Ready (cd.ready, Cooldowns): Is this ability's cooldown over (or never started)? In: Player Player, Team Team. Out: Ready Yes/No.
- Cooldown Time Left (cd.left, Cooldowns): Seconds until this ability's cooldown is over (0 when ready). In: Player Player, Team Team. Out: Seconds Number.
- Reset Cooldown (cd.reset, Cooldowns): Ends a cooldown now (the ability is ready again). In: Player Player, Team Team.
- Picked Up (item.picked_up, Events): Runs when a player picks a weapon or an item up from the ground (not when they buy one or the mode gives it). Item is its short name: ak47, kevlar, hegrenade... Out: Player Player, Item Text.
- Dropped (item.dropped, Events): Runs when a player drops a weapon (G, or the mode makes them). On death: also when a dying player's weapon falls. Out: Player Player, Weapon Text.
- Infinite Ammo (wpn.infinite_ammo, Weapons): Keeps a player's ammo full: the clip (no reloading), the spare ammo, or both. Reset on death: back to normal when they die. In: Player Player.
- Fire Rate (wpn.fire_rate, Weapons): Makes a player's guns fire faster (2 = twice as fast) or slower (0.5 = half). 1 is normal. Reset on death: back to 1 when they die. In: Player Player, Multiplier Number.
- Recoil (wpn.recoil, Weapons): Scales how much a player's view kicks when they fire: 0 none, 0.5 half, 1 normal, 2 double. Reset on death: back to 1 when they die. In: Player Player, Multiplier Number.
- Saved Text (save.text_get, Saved): Text kept for this player across maps, restarts and crashes (empty until set). Each mode has its own file. In: Player Player. Out: Text Text.
- Save Text (save.text_set, Saved): Keeps text for this player across maps and restarts (up to 63 letters). In: Player Player, Text Text.
- Server Value (save.server_get, Saved): A value kept for the whole server (not per player) across maps and restarts: a number and a text (each 0 or empty until set). Out: Number Number, Text Text.
- Set Server Value (save.server_set, Saved): Keeps a number or a text for the whole server across maps and restarts. In: Number Number, Text Text.
- Top Players (save.top, Saved): The best players by a saved value (Saved Value's name), highest first or lowest first, offline players too (the save file keeps their names): Each runs once per place with Rank, Name and Value, then Then. How many places: Top Players places, in the mode's Limits settings (10 to start). Out: Rank Number, Name Text, Value Number.
- Get Bone Position (ent.bone_pos, Entities): Where a bone of a player's or any model entity's skeleton is now (like Bip01 R Hand or Bip01 Head), and which way it points. Model is only for the list of bones; the bone is looked up by name in the model the entity really has, and Found is No when it has no such bone. Positions follow the server's animation: close, not pixel-exact. In: Entity Entity. Out: Position Vector, Angles Vector, Found Yes/No.
- Get Attachment Position (ent.attachment_pos, Entities): Where an attachment point of an entity's model is now (a gun's muzzle, a hand; models number them 0 to 3), and its angles. Model is only for the list; Found is No when the entity's real model has no such attachment. Positions follow the server's animation: close, not pixel-exact. In: Entity Entity. Out: Position Vector, Angles Vector, Found Yes/No.
- Players Pass Through Each Other (col.semiclip, Collision): Lets players walk through each other (semiclip): nobody, everyone, teammates only, or chosen players (each wired player set on or off; a chosen player passes through everyone). Bullets still hit. Turning it off nudges anyone left inside someone else free. Bots path as usual. In: Player (chosen players) Player.
- Set Entity Collision (col.set_solid, Collision): How a prop, an NPC or a spawned thing collides: solid (blocks and gets hit), trigger (things pass through, it still feels touches) or pass-through (nothing). Not for players (Players Pass Through Each Other is for them). In: Entity Entity. Out: Done Yes/No.
- Set Entity Size (col.set_size, Collision): The box an entity takes up, as mins and maxs from its origin (each min below its max). Not for players: their box is the game's. In: Entity Entity. Out: Done Yes/No.
- Entity Takes Damage (col.takes_damage, Collision): Whether a prop or an NPC can be hurt (on) or not (off). Not for players (Set God Mode is theirs). In: Entity Entity. Out: Done Yes/No.
- Entity Health (col.health, Collision): An entity's health (a prop, an NPC, a creature, a player). In: Entity Entity. Out: Health Number.
- Set Entity Health (col.set_health, Collision): Sets a prop's or an NPC's health (at least 1; to destroy it use its own damage or removal). Not for players (Set Health is theirs). In: Entity Entity, Health Number. Out: Done Yes/No.
- Spawn Trigger Volume (vol.spawn, Collision): An invisible box or sphere that tells you who goes in and out (Begin Overlap, End Overlap). Where: a Position, or At entity plus a Local offset (X forward, Y right, Z up by its facing) - attached, it follows the entity and turns with it. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) turns a box; a sphere ignores it. Size is its own setting; Velocity and Scale don't apply (a volume doesn't move by itself). Who counts: players, creatures or anything. Checked ten times a second (one search round each volume). A name lets Player Touched and the overlap events pick it out. Then runs right away whatever happened; Spawned or Failed says which, and Failure reason why (Out of entity slots, Limit reached: Trigger volumes at once in Limits, or Bad input: At entity is gone and there's no Position). It isn't solid, so it never checks the spot. In: Position Vector, Rotation Vector, At entity Entity, Local offset Vector. Out: Entity Trigger Volume, Success Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Remove Trigger Volume (vol.remove, Collision): Removes a trigger volume (whoever was inside gets End Overlap). In: Volume Entity.
- Is Overlapping (vol.is_overlapping, Collision): Is this entity (a player, a creature...) inside the trigger volume right now (and one its filter counts)? In: Volume Entity, Entity Entity. Out: Overlapping Yes/No.
- Begin Overlap (vol.on_begin, Events): Runs when something its filter counts goes into a trigger volume (Spawn Trigger Volume). Name: only volumes with this name (empty: any). Out: Volume Entity, Who Entity.
- End Overlap (vol.on_end, Events): Runs when something leaves a trigger volume (or the volume is removed, or it died or left the server inside). Name: only volumes with this name (empty: any). Out: Volume Entity, Who Entity.
- Entity Touched (col.on_touch, Events): Runs when an entity touches another (props, projectiles, NPCs, creatures, players; not the world's walls and floors). Name: only an entity with this name (empty: any). The first touch per N seconds for each entity (players standing on a prop would touch it every frame). Out: Entity Entity, Other Entity.
- Bullet Hit (col.on_bullet, Events): Runs where a shot lands: the shooter, the hit position, the surface's normal, what it hit (an entity, or World), the weapon and, on a player, where (head, chest...). At most once per shooter every N seconds (automatic weapons and shotguns would flood it). Out: Shooter Player, Hit Position Vector, Normal Vector, Hit Entity Entity, Hit World Yes/No, Weapon Text, Hit where Text.
- Bots Avoid Area (bots.avoid, Bots): Marks a place bots keep away from: a Position with a radius, or At entity (it rides along: a carrier, a burning player, a trigger volume; it ends when that's gone). Strength 1-10: 5 and up they won't stand in it, below they only path round it. Seconds: 0 till Bots Stop Avoiding. Which bots: every bot, or one team's (the carrier's own team can be left out). The same tag again moves or changes it. The bot brain keeps 32 at once. In: Position Vector, At entity Entity.
- Bots Stop Avoiding (bots.avoid_stop, Bots): Bots stop avoiding the place with this tag (Bots Avoid Area).
- Player Landed (col.on_landed, Events): Runs when a player lands after a fall: how fast they were falling (units a second; over 580 hurts) and the fall damage the game gives for it (0 if Fall Damage Off). Small hops don't count. Out: Player Player, Fall speed Number, Damage Number.
- Deal Damage (damage.deal, Damage): Hurts a player or any entity that can be hurt (a breakable, an NPC, a creature) by Amount, as if Attacker did it: kills, the kill feed, scores and Player Hurt / Player Killed count as usual. No Attacker: the world did it. Kind is what it counts as (a burn, a fall...); Hit zone is where (a head hit shows as a headshot in the kill feed; the amount isn't multiplied). Armor takes its share unless Ignore armor. In: Target Entity, Attacker Player, Amount Number.
- Get Entity Property (ent.prop_get, Entities): Reads a property of any entity (a prop, an NPC, a map entity, a player): its render mode, effect, color, amount, skin, body, scale, gravity, movement, collision, health or animation speed. Value is the number the game keeps (render modes and the like are numbered as in the map editor); Color is red, green, blue. In: Entity Entity. Out: Value Number, Color Vector.
- Set Entity Property (ent.prop_set, Entities): Changes a property of any entity: render mode, effect and color (so props and NPCs can glow or fade), amount, skin, body, scale, gravity, movement, collision, health or animation speed. Value is for the number properties; Pick is for the named ones (render mode, effect, movement, collision); Color for color. Players: render, color, skin, body, gravity and health work here; movement and collision are theirs to keep (use No Clip, Freeze). In: Entity Entity, Value Number, Color Vector.
- Big HUD Text (msg.big_hud, Messages): Big text on the screen (the director HUD: larger than HUD Text, its own slots), to one player or everyone, at a position (X and Y from 0 to 1; -1 centers), in a color, with an effect, for some seconds. A Value wired in goes after the text. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player, Value Anything.
- Colored Chat (msg.color_chat, Messages): A chat line in color, to one player or everyone: a green Tag first (empty: none), then the text in a team color (red, blue, gray, or the color of the player wired into Color of), green, or the usual yellow. A Value wired in goes after the text; color codes in a player's name or text never get through. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player, Value Anything, Color of Player.
- Player Movement State (player.move_state, Players): What a player is doing with their feet: on the ground, ducking, in water (and how deep: 0 dry, 1 feet, 2 waist, 3 under), on a ladder, and how fast (across the ground, and up or down: falling is negative). In: Player Player. Out: On ground Yes/No, Ducking Yes/No, In water Yes/No, Water level Number, On ladder Yes/No, Speed Number, Vertical speed Number.
- Push (player.push, Players): Pushes a player or an entity: along where they aim, where they face (flat), the Direction wired in, away from a Point, or straight up, by Strength (units a second). Add keeps their speed and adds to it; Replace sets it. Lift adds a little upward push so people on the ground aren't held by friction. Jump pads, dashes, knockback. In: Player or entity Entity, Direction Vector, Away from point Vector, Strength Number.
- Jump Rules (player.jump_rules, Players): Jumping rules for a player (or everyone): block jumping or ducking, extra jumps in the air (double jump and more), and automatic bunny hopping (hold jump to hop with no slowdown). Their own game predicts the stock moves, so a blocked jump can look like a small hop on their screen. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Grenade Thrown (event.grenade_thrown, Events): Runs when a player throws a grenade: who, the grenade (an entity: Set Grenade Fuse, Push, Remove Entity work on it), which kind and where. Type: only that kind. Out: Thrower Player, Grenade Entity, Kind Text, Position Vector.
- Grenade Exploded (event.grenade_exploded, Events): Runs when a thrown grenade goes off (a smoke grenade when it starts smoking): who threw it, the grenade, which kind and where. Type: only that kind. Out: Thrower Player, Grenade Entity, Kind Text, Position Vector.
- Set Grenade Fuse (ent.grenade_fuse, Entities): How many seconds until a thrown grenade goes off, from now (0: at once). Anything that isn't a thrown grenade is left alone. In: Grenade Entity, Seconds Number.
- Play Animation (ent.play_anim, Entities): Plays an animation (a sequence of its model, by name or number) on a prop, an NPC or any model entity, at a speed (1 normal), from the start or not; Loop plays a one-time animation again every Length seconds (looping ones loop by themselves). Players, creatures and NPCs that are walking are animated by the game and will switch back. In: Entity Entity, Sequence number Number.
- Attach To (ent.attach, Entities): Makes an entity (a prop, a sprite, an NPC) follow a player or another entity, keeping an offset (X forward is along the world, not their facing) or, at an attachment point of their model (0 to 3), following that point. It's let go when Detach runs, the parent is removed or dies (if asked), or the attached one is removed. In: Entity Entity, Parent Entity, Offset Vector.
- Detach (ent.detach, Entities): Lets go of an entity attached with Attach To; it stays where it is (or falls, if Fall is on). In: Entity Entity.
- On Map Entity Fired (event.map_fired, Events): Runs when a named entity of the map is triggered (by a button, a trigger, a timer or another entity) or used: its name, the entity, who set it off (a player, or nobody) and the entity that fired it. Name: only that entity (empty: any named one). Map logic drives the mode without an ls_event. Out: Entity name Text, Entity Entity, Activator Player, Caller Entity.
- Remove Map Objectives (game.remove_objectives, Game): Takes the map's objectives away (tick which): buy zones, bomb sites, hostages, hostage rescue zones, VIP safety zones, escape zones. The game notices at the next round (the bomb isn't given, no hostages to save); removed buy zones don't fall back to buying at spawn. Best at Map Started.
- Map Type (game.map_type, Game): What kind of map this is now: bomb (de_), hostage (cs_), VIP (as_), escape (es_) or other, from what it has in it; and each one as yes or no. Out: Type Text, Has bomb sites Yes/No, Has hostages Yes/No, Has VIP zone Yes/No, Has escape zone Yes/No.
- Weapon Switched (event.weapon_switched, Events): Runs when a player takes out a weapon (a switch, a pick-up that goes to hand, a spawn): the player, the new weapon and the one before (short names: ak47, knife; empty when there was none), and the weapon entity. Out: Player Player, New weapon Text, Old weapon Text, Weapon entity Entity.
- Voice Rules (game.voice_rules, Game): Who hears whom on voice chat: everyone, only teammates, the dead only the dead and the living only the living, or only those within a distance (0: any distance, with the other rules). Spectators hear spectators. Voice Override changes it for one player; Mute Voice still mutes.
- Voice Override (player.voice_override, Players): Changes the Voice Rules for one player: everyone hears them, nobody does, they hear everyone, or back to the rules. In: Player Player.
- Play Radio (msg.radio, Messages): Plays one of the game's radio lines or announcer words to a player, a team or everyone, with the radio text in chat (as From, if a player is wired in). Only the game's own sounds: nothing to load. In: Player Player, From Player.
- In Map Zone (player.in_zone, Players): Is a player in one of the map's zones now: a buy zone, a bomb site, a hostage rescue zone, an escape zone or a VIP safety zone (the map's own, as the game sees them). In: Player Player. Out: In it Yes/No.
- Entered Map Zone (event.zone_enter, Events): Runs when a living player walks into one of the map's zones (checked four times a second). Out: Player Player.
- Left Map Zone (event.zone_leave, Events): Runs when a living player walks out of one of the map's zones (checked four times a second). Out: Player Player.
- Show Info Window (msg.info_window, Messages): Opens the game's info window (the one the server's message of the day uses) for a player, with a title and text: Text from here, then any Text wired in (from a data table or Format Text). [br] starts a new line, [b]...[b] makes words bold. Plain text only: never a web page or a link. In: Player Player, Text Text.
- NPC Move To (npc.move_to, NPCs): Sends an NPC walking (or running) to an entity or a point now, along the map's bot navigation (straight when the map has none), facing where it goes. Arrived runs when it gets there, Failed when it can't (no way, stuck, or too long). Then it goes back to what it did, or stays there. In: NPC Entity, To entity Entity, Or point Vector.
- NPC Follow Path (npc.follow_path, NPCs): Sends an NPC along points in order: an array of positions, or a map's path_track chain by its first name. At point runs at each one, Finished at the end (never with Loop), Failed when it can't get on. Then it goes back to what it did, or stays there. In: NPC Entity, Points Array of Vector.
- NPC Stop (npc.stop, NPCs): Stops an NPC's Move To or Follow Path where it is (neither Arrived nor Failed runs); it goes back to what it did, or stays. In: NPC Entity.
- Round End Rules (game.round_end_rules, Game): Stops rounds ending by themselves: when a team is wiped out, when the time runs out, or either (End Round is then the only way a round ends). Ending as usual undoes it; a new mode starts as usual.
- Has Admin Flag (player.has_flag, Players): Does a player have this admin flag (from the server's admin list): kick, ban, change map, a custom level and so on. In: Player Player. Out: Has it Yes/No.
- Start Vote (game.start_vote, Game): Asks everyone (or a team, or the living) a question with 2 to 8 answers for some seconds; then runs the winning answer's output, Tie, or No votes. Bots vote at random if Bots vote is on. Only one vote at a time, and never over the server's map or mode vote (then No votes runs). Vote Count reads the result.
- Vote Count (game.vote_count, Game): How many votes an answer got in the last Start Vote (0: all the votes). In: Answer Number. Out: Votes Number.
- Hostage Follow (hostage.follow, NPCs): Makes a hostage follow a player (as if they pressed USE on it), any team. In: Hostage Entity, Leader Player.
- Hostage Stop (hostage.stop, NPCs): Makes a hostage stop following and wait where it is. In: Hostage Entity.
- Is Following (hostage.is_following, NPCs): Is a hostage following someone, and whom. In: Hostage Entity. Out: Following Yes/No, Leader Player.
- Add Bots (botctl.add, Bots): Adds bots through the bot brain's own commands: how many, to which team, how good (new bots only). Never more than the free slots (one is kept open for a person). The host's bot count comes back at the next map. In: How many Number.
- Remove Bots (botctl.remove, Bots): Takes bots off the server (of a team, or any), lowering the bot count so they don't come back this map. The host's bot count comes back at the next map. In: How many Number.
- Beam Between Entities (fx.beam_ents, Effects): A beam from one player or entity to another that follows both as they move, for some seconds. Effects are skipped (and the debugger says so) past 24 in one server frame, so many at once can't flood players' games. In: From Entity, To Entity.
- Icon Over Player (fx.icon_over, Effects): A sprite floating over a player's head (the game's own, like sprites/iplayervip.spr, or your own), for some seconds or until removed (0), seen by everyone, a team or only Viewer. Remove takes the icons off that player. In: Player Player, Viewer Player.
- Sprite At (fx.sprite_at, Effects): Shows a sprite once at a position or an entity (the game's own or your own), at a size and brightness. In: At Entity, Position Vector.
- Tracer (fx.tracer, Effects): A bullet tracer streak from one position to another. In: From Vector, To Vector.
- Radar Blip (hud.radar_blip, HUD & View): A dot on players' radar at a position or an entity (everyone's, a team's or only Viewer's), or takes it off. Hostage dots: four slots, each one dot (a hostage map's own hostages share the game's dots). Bomb dot: one, the dropped-bomb dot (the game moves it when the real bomb drops or is picked up). In: At Entity, Position Vector, Viewer Player.
- Show Team Score (hud.team_score, HUD & View): Shows a team's score on everyone's scoreboard (the number only: the game's own count of rounds won is unchanged and is shown again when the next round ends). In: Score Number.
- Set Weather (world.weather, World): Rain, snow or clear weather for everyone or one player, kept through respawns (Counter-Strike 1.6 and Condition Zero draw it; how much depends on the player's settings). In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Set Fog (world.fog, World): Fog of a color and thickness for everyone or one player (0 thickness: none), kept through respawns. It depends on the player's renderer: OpenGL draws it, software mode doesn't. In: Player (empty: everyone) Player.
- Dynamic Light (fx.dlight, Effects): A light that brightens what's around it for a moment: at a position, or following an entity (a player, a projectile) for the seconds given. Fade dims it over time (units a second; 0 stays bright until the end). Players see it in their own game. In: Follow (optional) Entity, At position Vector, Radius Number, Seconds Number, Fade (units a second) Number.
- Decal (fx.decal, Effects): Puts a decal (a scorch, blood, a bullet hole...) on the surface nearest a position: it looks six ways from the point within Reach and paints the closest wall, floor or ceiling, or a door it hits. The game's own decals; they fade like any decal. In: Near position Vector, Reach Number, Decal Decal.
- Break Into Gibs (fx.gibs, Effects): Pieces fly out from a position or an entity's middle, as when something breaks: wood, glass, metal, rocks, flesh, or your own model's parts (Custom model). Material is the sound they make. Size is how big the space they fly from is. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Pieces Number, Speed Number, Seconds Number, Size Number, Custom model (empty: the one above) Model.
- Beam Ring (fx.ring, Effects): A ring that grows out from a point, like a shockwave: radius, color, how long and how thick. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Radius Number, Seconds Number, Width Number.
- Play Sound 2D (snd.play_2d, Effects): A sound heard as is, not from a place: by one player, a team or everyone. Any sound: the game's own or yours. Volume 0 to 1, pitch 50 to 255 (100 normal). Map sounds are best mono: a stereo .wav is heard in the middle of your head, not from where it plays. Your own sounds (sound/custom/...wav) are loaded with the map and go with the mode when you publish it. In: Player Player, Volume Number, Pitch Number, Sound Sound.
- Play Sound at Location (snd.play_at, Effects): A sound from a place (a position, or where an entity is now), heard louder close by. Heard is how far it carries. Volume 0 to 1, pitch 50 to 255 (100 normal). Map sounds are best mono: a stereo .wav is heard in the middle of your head, not from where it plays. Your own sounds (sound/custom/...wav) are loaded with the map and go with the mode when you publish it. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Volume Number, Pitch Number, Sound Sound.
- Play Sound on Entity (snd.play_on, Effects): A sound that comes from an entity or a player and moves with it, on a channel (a new sound on the same channel replaces the last one). Volume 0 to 1, pitch 50 to 255 (100 normal). Map sounds are best mono: a stereo .wav is heard in the middle of your head, not from where it plays. Your own sounds (sound/custom/...wav) are loaded with the map and go with the mode when you publish it. In: Entity or player Entity, Volume Number, Pitch Number, Sound Sound.
- Loop Sound (snd.loop, Effects): A sound that keeps playing at a spot, or riding on an entity, until Stop Sound gets its Handle (or the round ends with the entity). A .wav with loop points loops by itself; for one without, set Play again every (seconds). How many play at once is a mode setting (Limits: Loop sounds at once, 16 to start). Map sounds are best mono: a stereo .wav is heard in the middle of your head, not from where it plays. Your own sounds (sound/custom/...wav) are loaded with the map and go with the mode when you publish it. In: On entity Entity, At position Vector, Volume Number, Pitch Number, Play again every (seconds) Number, Sound Sound. Out: Handle Sound Loop.
- Stop Sound (snd.stop, Effects): Stops a Loop Sound (its Handle), whatever plays on an entity's channel, or every sound a player hears now. In: Loop handle Entity, Entity Entity, Player Player.
- Spawn Entity (ent.spawn_entity, Entities): Makes one of the game's entities with your keys (key=value pairs as in a map, | between them: model=sprites/glow01.spr|rendercolor=255 0 0|targetname=door_fx). Only classes that are safe to make while the game runs are listed: effects, sounds, markers, relays, pickups. Never players, worldspawn, game_* server controls or anything that runs commands. Files its keys name are loaded with the map; if one isn't on the server it's skipped, never a crash. Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number. Out: Entity Entity, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Spawn Weapon On Ground (ent.spawn_weapon, Entities): A weapon or item lying on the ground, picked up like a map's own: any Counter-Strike gun, grenade, armor or the shield (the shield and the guns after the M249 in the list need Loner-Strike's game DLL). Reserve ammo is given with it on pickup (-1: the game's usual). Back after brings it back that many seconds after it's taken (0: at the next round, as the game does). Where: At entity (its spot, moved by Local offset along its own forward, right and up; it faces the way the entity does if Face the way At entity faces is on, turned by Rotation offset) or At position. Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) sets the facing outright; Velocity starts it moving (a still thing then falls and slides); Scale sizes models and sprites. If the spot is blocked (Unreal's Spawn Collision Handling): Always spawn, ignore collisions (Unreal's Always Spawn: it may get stuck); Try a nearby spot, but always spawn (Adjust If Possible But Always Spawn); Try a nearby spot, don't spawn if still blocked (Adjust If Possible But Don't Spawn If Colliding); Don't spawn if blocked (Do Not Spawn); or Retry every N seconds up to M tries (0: until it's clear). Nearby means within Max distance; Moved says it was moved. Outputs: Then goes on right away; Spawned once it exists, Failed once it gives up (Retry can make these come later); Entity, Success, Moved and Failure Reason (Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input) let you try a fallback, like another spot. In: At entity Entity, At position Vector, Local offset (forward, right, up) Vector, Rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) Vector, Rotation offset Vector, Velocity Vector, Scale Number, Reserve ammo Number, Back after (seconds) Number. Out: Entity Entity, Success Yes/No, Moved Yes/No, Failure reason Spawn Failure.
- Players In Radius (spatial.players_in_radius, Spatial): Every player within Radius of a point or an entity, as an array (an entity wired in isn't counted itself). In: Around point Vector, Around entity Entity, Radius Number. Out: Players Array of Player.
- Nearest Player (spatial.nearest_player, Spatial): The player nearest to a point or an entity (not the entity itself), within Max distance; nobody if none. In: Around point Vector, Around entity Entity. Out: Player Player, Distance Number.
- Entities In Radius (spatial.entities_in_radius, Spatial): Entities within Radius of a point or an entity, of a class or any, as an array (up to the mode's Limits setting, 64 at first). Players aren't listed (use Players In Radius). In: Around point Vector, Around entity Entity, Radius Number. Out: Entities Array of Entity.
- Nearest Entity (spatial.nearest_entity, Spatial): The entity of a class nearest to a point or an entity, within Max distance; nothing if none. Players aren't counted. In: Around point Vector, Around entity Entity. Out: Entity Entity, Distance Number.
- Line of Sight (spatial.line_of_sight, Spatial): Is there a clear line between A and B (each an entity or a point)? Entities wired in don't block it (a player's eyes are used). Hit Position is where something got in the way. In: A Entity, Or point A Vector, B Entity, Or point B Vector. Out: Clear Yes/No, Hit position Vector.
- Random Chance (random.chance, Numbers): Yes Percent % of the time (a new roll each time it's worked out). In: Percent Number. Out: Yes Yes/No.
- Random Bool (random.bool, Numbers): Yes or no, half the time each. Out: Yes Yes/No.
- Weighted Random Pick (random.weighted, Numbers): Picks an index from an array of weights (a weight of 3 is picked three times as often as 1); with Items wired, the item at that index too. -1 when every weight is 0. In: Weights Array of Number, Items Array of the node's type. Out: Index Number, Item The node's type.
- Map Range (math.map_range, Numbers): A value from one range moved into another: In Min..In Max becomes Out Min..Out Max (Clamp keeps it inside). In: Value Number, In Min Number, In Max Number, Out Min Number, Out Max Number. Out: Result Number.
- Sin / Cos / Tan (math.trig, Numbers): The sine, cosine or tangent of an angle (degrees, or radians). In: Angle Number. Out: Result Number.
- Atan2 (math.atan2, Numbers): The angle of the direction X, Y (from the X axis, -180..180 degrees, or radians). In: Y Number, X Number. Out: Angle Number.
- Degrees / Radians (math.angle_convert, Numbers): Degrees to radians or radians to degrees. In: Angle Number. Out: Result Number.
- Nearly Equal (flow.nearly_equal, Conditions): Are A and B within Tolerance of each other (for numbers that came out of math, which are seldom exactly equal)? In: A Number, B Number, Tolerance Number. Out: Nearly equal Yes/No.
- Split Text (text.split, Text): Text cut at each Separator, as an array of texts (at most 64 pieces; empty pieces kept). In: Text Text, Separator Text. Out: Pieces Array of Text.
- Replace Text (text.replace, Text): The text with every Find replaced by With (capitals matter). In: Text Text, Find Text, With Text. Out: Text Text.
- Substring (text.substring, Text): Part of the text: Length characters from Start (the first is 0). In: Text Text, Start Number, Length Number. Out: Text Text.
- Upper Case (text.upper, Text): THE TEXT IN CAPITALS. In: Text Text. Out: Text Text.
- Lower Case (text.lower, Text): the text in small letters. In: Text Text. Out: Text Text.
- Trim Text (text.trim, Text): The text without spaces at the start and end. In: Text Text. Out: Text Text.
- Starts With (text.starts_with, Text): Does the text start with this (capitals don't matter)? In: Text Text, Start Text. Out: Starts with Yes/No.
- Ends With (text.ends_with, Text): Does the text end with this (capitals don't matter)? In: Text Text, End Text. Out: Ends with Yes/No.
- Join Array (text.join, Text): An array's texts in one, with Separator between them (as much as fits in 127 characters). In: Texts Array of Text, Separator Text. Out: Text Text.
- Format Time (text.format_time, Text): Seconds as a clock: 1:05, or 1:02:05 (Auto: hours only when there are any). In: Seconds Number. Out: Text Text.
- Format Number (text.format_number, Text): A number as text with a set number of decimals, and thousands separated by commas if you like (12,345.6). In: Number Number. Out: Text Text.
- Sum (array.sum, Arrays): All the numbers added up (0 for an empty array). In: Numbers Array of Number. Out: Sum Number.
- Array Min (array.min, Arrays): The smallest number, and its index (-1 for an empty array). In: Numbers Array of Number. Out: Min Number, Index Number.
- Array Max (array.max, Arrays): The biggest number, and its index (-1 for an empty array). In: Numbers Array of Number. Out: Max Number, Index Number.
- Average (array.average, Arrays): The numbers' average (0 for an empty array). In: Numbers Array of Number. Out: Average Number.
- Reverse (array.reverse, Arrays): Turns an array round: the last item first. In: Array Array of the node's type.
- Slice (array.slice, Arrays): A new array with Count items from Start (the first is 0). In: Array Array of the node's type, Start Number, Count Number. Out: Array Array of the node's type.
- Dot Product (vec.dot, Vectors): A·B: how much two directions point the same way (with both length 1: 1 same, 0 square, -1 opposite). In: A Vector, B Vector. Out: Dot Number.
- Cross Product (vec.cross, Vectors): A×B: the direction square to both (its length is how far apart they point). In: A Vector, B Vector. Out: Cross Vector.
- Random Point In Radius (vec.random_in_radius, Vectors): A random point within Radius of Center: on a flat circle (2D, Z kept) or in a ball (3D). In: Center Vector, Radius Number. Out: Point Vector.
- Rotate Vector (vec.rotate, Vectors): Turns a vector round the vertical by Yaw degrees (and up or down by Pitch). In: Vector Vector, Yaw Number, Pitch Number. Out: Result Vector.
- Lerp Vector (vec.lerp, Vectors): A point between A and B: Alpha 0 is A, 1 is B, 0.5 halfway. In: A Vector, B Vector, Alpha Number. Out: Result Vector.
- Direction To Angles (vec.to_angles, Vectors): A direction as angles (pitch, yaw, 0), for aiming and Look At math. In: Direction Vector. Out: Angles Vector.
- Angles To Forward Vector (vec.forward, Vectors): Angles (pitch, yaw, roll) as the direction they face, length 1. In: Angles Vector. Out: Direction Vector.
- To Local Space (rel.to_local, Vectors): A world position as seen from a player or entity: X forward, Y right, Z up (by its facing; a player's view yaw). In: Player or entity Entity, World position Vector. Out: Local offset Vector.
- To World Space (rel.to_world, Vectors): An offset from a player or entity (X forward, Y right, Z up, by its facing) as a world position. In: Player or entity Entity, Local offset Vector. Out: World position Vector.
- Relative Position Of (rel.position_of, Vectors): How far B is in front of, to the right of and above A (by A's facing; behind and left are negative). In: A Entity, B Entity. Out: Forward Number, Right Number, Up Number.
- Angle To (rel.angle_to, Vectors): How far A would turn to face B: the yaw difference, -180..180 degrees (positive: to the left). In: A Entity, B Entity. Out: Angle Number.
- Is In Front (rel.is_in_front, Vectors): Is B in front of A, inside a cone of this many degrees round A's facing? In: A Entity, B Entity. Out: In front Yes/No.
- Is Behind (rel.is_behind, Vectors): Is B behind A, inside a cone of this many degrees round A's back (backstabs, sneaking)? In: A Entity, B Entity. Out: Behind Yes/No.
- Eye Position (aim.eye_pos, Players): Where a player's eyes are (their position plus view height). In: Player Player. Out: Eyes Vector.
- Aim Direction (aim.dir, Players): Which way a player is aiming, length 1 (from their view angles). In: Player Player. Out: Direction Vector.
- Aim Point (aim.point, Players): What a player is aiming at, up to Max distance: where the line from their eyes hits, the entity hit, the surface's normal, and whether it hit anything (the player is ignored). In: Player Player. Out: Hit position Vector, Hit entity Entity, Hit normal Vector, Hit Yes/No.
- Multi Gate (flow.multi_gate, Flow): Each time flow comes in, goes out the next output (in order, or random); after the last it stops, or starts over with Loop. Reset starts again from Start index.
- Do Once Per Player (flow.do_once_per_player, Flow): Lets the flow through once for each player, until Reset (everyone) or Reset Player (the player wired in then). In: Player Player.
- Toggle Variable (var.toggle, Variables): Flips a yes/no variable (yes becomes no, no becomes yes); New Value is what it is now. A per-player one needs a Player, a per-team one a Team. In: Player Player, Team Team. Out: New value Yes/No.
- On Tick (event.on_tick, Events): Runs again and again, every Interval seconds (0.1: ten times a second; 0: as often as the mode's Limits setting lets it, 100 a second at first), all through the map. Delta is the seconds since the last time. Out: Delta Number.
- Draw Debug Line (debug.draw_line, Advanced): Draws a line from A to B for some seconds, to see where things are. Shown only while testing (Playtest and Test run); a finished mode draws nothing. In: From Vector, To Vector.
- Draw Debug Box (debug.draw_box, Advanced): Draws a box between two opposite corners for some seconds. Shown only while testing (Playtest and Test run); a finished mode draws nothing. In: Corner Vector, Opposite corner Vector.
- Draw Debug Point (debug.draw_point, Advanced): Draws a small box round a point for some seconds. Shown only while testing (Playtest and Test run); a finished mode draws nothing. In: Position Vector.
- Log Line (debug.log_line, Messages): Writes a line to the AMX Mod X log (addons/amxmodx/logs), up to Most a second (that setting's number of lines) from this node; the rest are counted in the next line. In: Text Text.
- Bitwise (math.bitwise, Numbers): Bits of whole numbers (the fractions are dropped): And, Or, Xor, Not (of A), or A shifted left or right by B bits. Exact up to 16,777,216. In: A Number, B Number. Out: Result Number.
- Find Free Spot Near (spatial.free_spot, Spatial): A spot near a point where a player (or the hull you pick) fits: the point itself if it's free, else the nearest free one in rings round it, up to Max distance (at most the mode's Limits setting of tries, 64 at first). Found is no when there's none (Position is then the point). In: Near Vector. Out: Found Yes/No, Position Vector.
- Player Language (player.language, Players): A player's language: AMX Mod X's for them (their lang setting, else the server's, like en), or their game's (cl_language, like english: empty for bots, and for a moment until their game answers). In: Player Player. Out: Language Text.
- As NPC (cast.npc, NPCs): Casting: is this entity an NPC (ls_npc, gm_components)? Success with it as that kind, else Failed. The one-click fix where an Entity wire goes into a pin of that kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: NPC NPC.
- As Projectile (cast.projectile, Projectiles): Casting: is this entity a projectile (Spawn Projectile's)? Success with it as that kind, else Failed. The one-click fix where an Entity wire goes into a pin of that kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: Projectile Projectile.
- As Trigger Volume (cast.volume, Collision): Casting: is this entity a trigger volume (Spawn Trigger Volume's)? Success with it as that kind, else Failed. The one-click fix where an Entity wire goes into a pin of that kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: Trigger Volume Trigger Volume.
- As Objective Marker (cast.objmarker, Effects): Casting: is this entity an objective marker? Success with it as that kind, else Failed. The one-click fix where an Entity wire goes into a pin of that kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: Objective Marker Objective Marker.
- As Component (cast.component, Components): Casting: is this entity one of gm_components' components (any kind)? Success with it as that kind, else Failed. The one-click fix where an Entity wire goes into a pin of that kind. In: Entity Entity. Out: Component Component.
- Set Entity Transform (ent.set_transform, Entities): Puts an entity where a Transform says: its Position, Rotation, Scale (props and sprites; players can't be resized) and Velocity. In: Entity Entity, Transform Transform.
- Color (color.literal, Colors): A color picked with the color picker (and how opaque: alpha). Out: Color Color.
- Make Color (color.make, Colors): A color from red, green, blue and alpha (0 to 255 each). In: Red Number, Green Number, Blue Number, Alpha Number. Out: Color Color.
- Break Color (color.break, Colors): A color's red, green, blue and alpha (0 to 255 each). In: Color Color. Out: Red Number, Green Number, Blue Number, Alpha Number.
- Blend Colors (color.lerp, Colors): Between color A (Amount 0) and color B (Amount 1): 0.5 is halfway. In: A Color, B Color, Amount Number. Out: Color Color.
- Color From Hue (color.hsv, Colors): A color from hue (0 to 360: red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta), saturation and brightness (0 to 1). In: Hue Number, Saturation Number, Brightness Number. Out: Color Color.
- Model (asset.model, Files): A model file (models/....mdl), loaded with the map. Files are picked, never made from text: the game loads every file a mode can use before the map starts. Keep it in a variable, an array or a Function's input like any value. Out: Model Model.
- Sprite (asset.sprite, Files): A sprite file (sprites/....spr), loaded with the map. Files are picked, never made from text: the game loads every file a mode can use before the map starts. Keep it in a variable, an array or a Function's input like any value. Out: Sprite Sprite.
- Sound (asset.sound, Files): A sound file (a .wav from inside sound/), loaded with the map. Files are picked, never made from text: the game loads every file a mode can use before the map starts. Keep it in a variable, an array or a Function's input like any value. Out: Sound Sound.
- File Name Of (asset.file_name, Files): A Model's, Sprite's or Sound's file name as text (models/....mdl; a sound from inside sound/), to show or log it. Empty when it's none. In: File Anything. Out: Name Text.
- Decal (asset.decal, Files): A kind of decal from the game's decals.wad (bullet hole, scorch, blood...): keep it in a variable or an array, and wire it into Place Decal, which picks one of that kind. Out: Decal Decal.

## Game Mode Studio pin types (compact)

A wire joins the same type, or a narrower into a wider one (Goes into); the other way takes a cast node.

- Flow (exec): The white arrows: the order things run in. It carries no value. Cast: As Player, As Creature, As NPC, As Projectile, As Trigger Volume, As Objective Marker, As Component.
- Number (number): A number, with or without a fraction. A pin marked # takes a whole number: a fraction is rounded (and Problems says so for one you typed in).
- Yes/No (bool): Yes or no. Branch, the conditions and the gates use it.
- Text (text): Words: names, messages, map names. It doesn't last through a Delay unless it's kept in a variable. Cast: As Creature.
- Vector (vector): Three numbers, X, Y and Z: a place in the map, a direction or a speed. It doesn't last through a Delay unless it's kept in a variable.
- Team (team): A team: Terrorists or Counter-Terrorists (no team for a draw).
- Timer (timer): A timer a Delay, Repeat or Countdown started, to stop or check later.
- Color (color): A color, picked with the color picker (red, green and blue).
- Anything (any): A pin that takes a value of any type, like the value shown by Show HUD Text.
- Player (player): A player in the game: a person or a bot. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Player.
- Entity (entity): Anything in the world: a player, a prop, a creature, an NPC, a component, a map entity. The handles below are entities known to be one kind.
- NPC (npc): An NPC from Spawn NPC: a person who talks, walks paths and follows. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As NPC.
- Creature (creature): A creature from Spawn Creature: it moves, attacks and can be hurt. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Creature.
- Projectile (projectile): A projectile from Spawn Projectile, flying until it hits or expires. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Projectile.
- Trigger Volume (volume): A trigger volume from Spawn Trigger Volume: an invisible box that notices who goes in and out. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Trigger Volume.
- Objective Marker (objmarker): An objective marker: a sprite floating over an entity or a spot, until Remove Marker. Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Objective Marker.
- Component (component): A component the mode made or the map placed: a capture point, a shop, a barricade, a door… Goes into: Entity. Cast: As Component.
- Sound Loop (soundloop): A sound that keeps playing (Loop Sound) until Stop Sound gets it. Goes into: Entity.
- Model (model): A model file (.mdl) the mode loads: props, creatures, attachments. Your own go with the mode. Goes into: Model or Sprite.
- Sprite (sprite): A sprite file (.spr): effects, glows, markers. Your own go with the mode. Goes into: Model or Sprite.
- Sound (sound): A sound file (.wav) the mode plays. Your own go with the mode.
- Decal (decal): A kind of decal from the game's decals.wad (a bullet hole, a scorch, blood).
- Model or Sprite (visual): A pin that takes a Model or a Sprite.
- Enum (enum): A value from a fixed list of named choices: the app's own lists below, or your mode's own enums.
- Struct (struct): A bundle of named values kept together: Transform, or your mode's own structs. It doesn't last through a Delay unless it's kept in a variable.
- Array (array): A list of values of one type, in order. An array doesn't go into an array of a wider type (an Array of Creatures isn't an Array of Entities): a value written through the wider type could be the wrong kind.
- Map (map): Values looked up by a key: text, a number or a player.
- Variable (var): A variable node's pin: it takes the type of the variable picked.
- Generic pins (generic): A pin whose type the node takes from a setting or from the first wire: an array node set to Players has Player pins.
- Entity Kind (enum:ls_kind): What an entity is. Values: Player, Bot, Creature, NPC, Interactable, Component, Prop, Map entity, None.
- Component Kind (enum:ls_comp_kind): Which kind of component it is. Values: Capture point, Extraction zone, Checkpoint, Shop, Barricade, Trap, Loot container, Supply drop, Supply crate, Perk machine, Upgrade bench, Mystery box, Meeting point, Moving platform, Timed door, Wave spawner, Safe zone, Shrinking zone, Damage zone, Weapon spawner, Respawn point, Player class, Pickup, NPC, Interactable, None.
- Spawn Failure (enum:ls_spawn_fail): Why a spawn failed: a spawn node's Failure reason. Values: None, Blocked, Out of entity slots, Limit reached, Missing file, Retries used up, Bad input.
- Who (enum:ls_who): Which players a For Each Player or Pick Random Player goes through. Values: Everyone in the game, Everyone alive, Everyone dead, Terrorists, Counter-Terrorists, Living Terrorists, Living Counter-Terrorists, Bots, People (not bots).
- Weapon (enum:ls_weapon): A weapon, by its game name. Goes into: Text. Values: none, ak47, m4a1, awp, scout, famas, galil, aug, sg552, mp5navy, p90, ump45, mac10, tmp, m3, xm1014, m249, deagle, usp, glock18, p228, fiveseven, elite, hegrenade, flashbang, smokegrenade, knife, c4, g3sg1, sg550.
- Hit Zone (enum:ls_hitzone): Where a hit landed on the body. Values: generic, head, chest, stomach, left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg.
- Damage Kind (enum:ls_dmgkind): What kind of damage it was. Values: other, shot, slash, blast, burn, fall, shock, drown, poison.
- Transform (struct:ls_transform): Where something is and how it moves, in one value. Fields: Position, Rotation, Scale, Velocity.

## Map editor entities (compact)

- button_target: A target to shoot: each hit switches it on or off, sets off its target as On or Off, and flips its texture (use a +0 / +a texture pair). Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, spawnflags.
- env_bubbles: Bubbles rising from inside the brush. Keys: targetname, density, current.
- func_bomb_target: A bomb site: Terrorists plant the bomb inside. Keys: targetname, target.
- func_breakable: Breaks when shot or set off (glass, crates, vents). Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, health, explosion, gibmodel, explodemagnitude, spawnflags.
- func_button: A button players press (or shoot) to set something off. Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, master, killtarget, delay, angle, speed, lip, sounds, spawnflags.
- func_buyzone: Where a team can buy. If a map has none, spawns get buy zones. Keys: target, team.
- func_conveyor: A conveyor belt: moves what stands on it and scrolls its texture. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, speed, spawnflags.
- func_door: A door that slides along its facing when touched or set off. Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, killtarget, delay, speed, lip, movesnd, stopsnd, health, spawnflags, angle.
- func_door_rotating: A door that swings round an origin brush. Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, killtarget, delay, speed, lip, movesnd, stopsnd, health, distance, spawnflags.
- func_escapezone: Where Terrorists escape to on an es_ map. Keys: none.
- func_friction: Changes how slippery the floor is. Keys: modifier.
- func_grencatch: Sets something off when a grenade lands inside. Keys: targetname, target, triggerongrenade.
- func_guntarget: A target that slides along path_corners when set off; shoot it enough and it stops and sets off its target. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, target, health, spawnflags.
- func_healthcharger: A wall unit players hold use on to heal. Give it a charger texture. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, health.
- func_hostage_rescue: Where Counter-Terrorists bring hostages. Keys: targetname, target.
- func_illusionary: Looks solid but you walk through it (leaves, fences, light shafts). Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, skin.
- func_ladder: A ladder players climb. Usually covered in the AAATRIGGER texture behind a ladder-looking brush. Keys: none.
- func_pendulum: Swings back and forth. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, speed, damp, spawnflags.
- func_plat: A lift that goes up and down. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, height, spawnflags.
- func_platrot: A lift that turns as it goes up and down. Needs an origin brush. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, movesnd, stopsnd, volume, height, speed.
- func_pushable: A crate players can push. Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, health, explosion, gibmodel, explodemagnitude, friction, size, spawnflags.
- func_recharge: A wall unit players hold use on for armor. Give it a charger texture. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, armorvalue.
- func_rot_button: A button that turns (a valve or wheel). Keys: targetname, target, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, master, delay, speed, distance.
- func_rotating: Spins all the time (fans, wheels). Needs an origin brush. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, angles, speed, spawnflags.
- func_tank: A gun turret: on its own it shoots at any player it sees (any team), or players take control from a func_tankcontrols. Build it facing east with an origin brush at the pivot. Bots don't use turrets. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, angles, yawrange, pitchrate, pitchtolerance, persistence, maxRange, barrel, barrelz, spritesmoke, rotatesound, spawnflags, bullet, bullet_damage.
- func_tankcontrols: Where players take control of a turret: press use inside, aim with the mouse, fire with attack, use again to let go. Keys: target.
- func_tanklaser: A laser turret: fires an env_laser (named below) where it aims. Build it facing east with an origin brush at the pivot. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, angles, yawrange, pitchrate, pitchtolerance, persistence, maxRange, barrel, barrelz, spritesmoke, rotatesound, spawnflags, laserentity.
- func_tankmortar: A mortar turret: each shot is an explosion where it aims. Build it facing east with an origin brush at the pivot. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, angles, yawrange, pitchrate, pitchtolerance, persistence, maxRange, barrel, barrelz, spritesmoke, rotatesound, spawnflags, iMagnitude.
- func_trackautochange: Like func_trackchange, but it moves by itself when the train arrives on it. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, movesnd, stopsnd, volume, train, bottomtrack, rotation, spawnflags.
- func_trackchange: A piece of track that moves or turns, with the train on it, to join another track (a turntable, a train lift). Set it off to move it. Needs an origin brush. Keys: targetname, rendermode, renderamt, renderfx, zhlt_lightflags, light_origin, movesnd, stopsnd, volume, train, bottomtrack, rotation, spawnflags.
